NCA officers arrested an Indian national, 38, on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations and he was taken into custody.

News.title: Murder investigation after man found dead and child seriously injured
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a man was found dead alongside a seriously injured child in County Tyrone on Saturday morning.

A male has been arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder and remains in custody.

The incident took place in Lisnahull Road in Dungannon.

The child was taken to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children.

Police are currently at the scene and have said the public should avoid the area while enquiries continue.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) said they received a 999 call at 11:08 BST on Saturday, following reports of an incident.

They dispatched a helicopter crew, three emergency crews, one advanced care paramedic, two ambulance officers and one HART (Hazardous Area Response Team) crew to the scene.

News.title: Woman detained in Egypt over 'sister's activism'
News.content:
A mother-of-four from Birmingham has been detained by the Egyptian authorities, with her husband and lawyer claiming it is due to her sister's online activism.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, from Handsworth Wood, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo in the early hours of Monday 17 August. Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said this was 24 hours after Egyptian security forces "ram-raided" the property and told her: "You need to tell your sister to stop".

Three of el-Shazly's other siblings have also been detained, with her two brothers already being held when she was taken, and one of her sisters detained soon after.

The BBC has contacted the Egyptian consulate in London but has not had a response.

Moustapha said: "The family's a bit traumatised. [The children] are heartbroken.

"We really need the UK government to get their fingers out as quickly as possible."

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) said: "We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt, and are in contact with the authorities."

News.title: Attempted murder arrest after man falls from balcony
News.content:
A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a man fell from a balcony.

Police were called to reports that the man had fallen at flats on Liverpool Street in Salford shortly after midnight on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said.

Emergency services attended and the man was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries, where he remains in a critical condition, the force said.

A man in his 20s has been taken into police custody for questioning.

The incident has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) because the men had earlier contact with police, GMP said.

A blue forensic tent has been erected near to a building on the corner of Liverpool Street and Southern Street.

A local resident, who did not wish to be named, said she heard sirens overnight and saw the aftermath of the incident being live-streamed on social media.

She said: "I heard all the sirens, but I keep myself to myself so I didn't go out.

"I've seen it's all cordoned off and there's a blue forensics tent.

"It's sad, it's really sad. It's a bit close to home."

Ch Insp Lee Gridley said: "A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, and he is currently being questioned in custody.

"Our officers are working at pace to establish the full circumstances, and a scene will remain in place whilst the investigation continues.

"We understand that incidents of this nature may cause concern within the community, however we believe this is an isolated incident and that there is no wider risk to the public."

An IOPC spokesperson said: "After being notified by the Greater Manchester Police of the previous police contact with the parties involved in this incident, we sent investigators to the police post-incident procedures in Manchester in assessment mode to gather further information.

"We continue to remain in assessment mode and will assess a GMP referral in due course."

News.title: Mountain of broken fridges growing across England and Wales
News.content:
A mountain of broken fridges is building up in waste centres across England and Wales, the Local Government Association (LGA) has warned.

This year's multiple heat waves have increased the numbers of white goods such as fridges and freezers breaking down and needing to be scrapped at specialist sites.

Dozens of councils have been forced to stop collections of white goods due to a major backlog, which has built up due to a national shortage of specialists needed to safely process the appliances.

Earlier this month, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the latest crackdown on illegal waste dumps - and the LGA is now calling on the government to take urgent action on dealing with white goods too.

LGA Neighbourhoods committee chair Councillor Arooj Shah called on the government to force white goods companies to pick up the burden, help councils with the cost of extra storage, and prevent the same problems recurring in future.

"The backlog of defunct white goods is getting bigger by the day â they're at risk of becoming a mountain," he said.

"It is not right that residents who are trying to do the right thing can't take old or broken appliances to their local recycling centre due to failures elsewhere in the system."

Councils from Bradford to Gloucestershire, Durham and Nottinghamshire are among 26 to have suspended fridge collections this month.

A Department for Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) spokesman acknowledged the capacity issues and said short-term storage was being set up.

He said: "Our priority is to minimise disruption to household collection or proper disposal of fridges and other cooling equipment, and we are pushing producers of these items to take all necessary steps to achieve this and resolve any collection delays."

Tom Cruise will reprise his role as NASCAR driver Cole Trickle in a follow-up to “Days of Thunder.”

Cruise made the announcement from Daytona International Speedway on Saturday, hours before NASCAR's regular-season finale. Anne Hathaway will co-star as a team owner and engineer in the film scheduled to be released by Paramount Pictures on June 2, 2028.

Cruise will serve as a producer alongside Jerry Bruckheimer and Tommy Harper. Jonathan Levine is set to direct the script written by Will Staples.

The Hollywood Reporter reported in November 2024 that Cruise had talked to Paramount about a follow-up to his 1990 NASCAR racing film. The original was a critically panned summer blockbuster that was largely lampooned throughout the NASCAR industry for its exaggeration and overindulgence.

It has since become a cult favorite in NASCAR circles and is still quoted by race fans to this day.

“Rubbin’, son, is racin’” — the immortal line from crew chief Harry Hogge, played by Robert Duvall — lives on.

Riding high from his “Top Gun” fame, Cruise had an idea for a movie based on fast cars and the characters who raced them. And so began the making of “Days of Thunder.”

Cole Trickle was loosely based on the late NASCAR driver Tim Richmond. Four-time Cup Series champion Jeff Gordon, now vice chairman at Hendrick Motorsports, has openly lobbied for Cruise to bring a “Days of Thunder” sequel to life.

Gordon and Cruise have become friends over the years — Cruise showed up at a 2015 NASCAR banquet to honor the retiring Gordon — which could boost the prospect of Gordon and Hendrick Motorsports’ involvement in a sequel.

The movie introduced NASCAR to a wider audience that had very limited exposure to stock-car racing before that summer. There had been racing movies before — think “Thunder Road,” “Grand Prix,” “Stroker Ace,” or even “Smokey and the Bandit” — but none that had depicted NASCAR in such a mainstream style.

NASCAR has seen more swings and misses than checkered flags when it comes to its portrayal on the big or small screen since “Days of Thunder.” For every “Talladega Nights,” there are 10 more bombs such as comedian Kevin James’ ill-fated Netflix’s comedy series, “ The Crew.”

News.title: Itauma vs Hrgovic LIVE: Start time, card, channel, fight updates and results tonight
News.content:
Heavyweight Moses Itauma on why he doesn't like partying as his star rises

Tonight, Moses Itauma has the chance to collect his first world heavyweight title, as he faces Filip Hrgovic in a fascinating main event.

At London’s O2 Arena, Itauma puts his unbeaten record on the line as he aims to pick up the IBF belt, which was recently vacated by Oleksandr Usyk. If the 21-year-old wins, he will become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion ever, after the legendary Mike Tyson.

Itauma isn’t the only one fighting for a full world title for the first time, though. The summit of Hrgovic’s career until now was a 2024 clash with Daniel Dubois, with the interim IBF belt on the line, and the Briton handed the Croat his only professional loss.

Since then, 34-year-old Hrgovic has gone 3-0, with all of those wins coming against British names. Can he add Itauma to the list? Or will the young sensation fulfil his world-title prophecy?

Follow live updates and results from Itauma vs Hrgovic and the undercard, below.

News.title: Tottenham v Newcastle LIVE: Spurs in dire straits again after back-to-back Premier League losses
News.content:
( Getty )

Tottenham are in dire straits once again after Newcastle inflicted a second straight Premier League loss on Roberto De Zerbi’s side.

Off the back of last weekend’s disastrous opening loss at Brentford, Spurs succumbed to second-half goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa, who continue to look like different players under new Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle.

Omar Marmoush had chances to score on his Tottenham debut but failed to convert, while Savio was notable for his absence due to muscular fatigue off the back of his impressive midweek cameo against Charlton.

The defeat will feel most bitter for former Newcastle man Sandro Tonali, who moved to Spurs for £100m in the summer and was jeered off by the away fans when he was substituted, following an unremarkable performance.

Six-time grand tour champion and Vuelta a Espana leader Tadej Pogacar has abandoned the race after a nasty crash on stage eight.

The two-time world champion was the overwhelming favourite to win the Vuelta, the only grand tour he has yet to win, and won three stages in its opening week. He led the race by nearly four minutes from Movistar’s Enric Mas before his shock crash and abandon with 31km to go on stage eight.

The race leader appeared to hit a rock as he swerved suddenly while travelling in the midst of the peloton along a wide road. He crashed hard, with riders falling around and behind him.

He sustained a nasty wound to his left shoulder and the left side of his face, with blood pouring from above his eye and his shoulder, and was immediately attended to by medical staff.

The Slovenian got up unassisted and attempted to get back on his bike before shaking his head and sitting down again in evident pain, before he was helped into a waiting ambulance by staff and taken immediately to hospital.

His UAE Team Emirates-XRG team have provided an update on his status of his injuries, with medical director Dr Adrian Rotunno confirming: “He is stable, and following a thorough medical assessment at hospital, Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions.

“Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout. He will require clavicle surgery which will be delayed due to concussion precautions. Tadej remains under the care of our medical team and we’ll provide further updates following the surgery.”

This is the first time Pogacar has abandoned a grand tour in 10 attempts, the first time he has ever not finished on the podium, and his first withdrawal from a race since breaking his wrist in a crash at Liege-Bastogne-Liege in 2023.

The 27-year-old won this year’s Tour de France in dominant fashion and carried that form into an electric first week at the Vuelta, winning stages one, four and six on his way to establishing a seemingly unassailable lead.

But his crash on an innocuous-seeming stretch of road on the way to Xeraco - reminiscent of his rival Jonas Vingegaard’s unexpected crash on stage 15 of this year’s Tour - blows the race wide open.

Spain’s Mas now leads the overall standings by one minute from Slovenia’s four-time champion Primoz Roglic, with Giro d’Italia runner-up Felix Gall third at 1’11”. Britain’s Oscar Onley leads the best young rider classification and now sits fifth, 2’16” off the pace.

open image in gallery Pogacar won three stages in the opening week ( Reuters )

Pogacar’s withdrawal also entirely changes the dynamic of the race. His UAE Team Emirates-XRG squad will now target stage wins through the likes of Joao Almeida and Jay Vine, while Visma-Lease a Bike, who had largely been expected to aim for stages through Wout van Aert and British rider Matthew Brennan, may now prioritise the general classification hopes of Sepp Kuss. The American won this race in 2023 and now sits fourth overall.

Solo breakaway rider Xabier Mikel Azparren was caught with just 1.5km to go on the technical run-in to the line in Xeraco, with a huge crash bringing down riders all over the road in a chaotic final sprint.

Two-time stage winner Brennan was momentarily boxed in and had too much ground to make up in the finale as Bryan Coquard of Cofidis won the sprint from Lidl-Trek’s Mads Pedersen for his first-ever grand tour stage win.

The race continues on Sunday with a mountainous 187.4km ride in the Costa Blanca, from La Vila Joiosa to the category-one summit finish atop Alto de Aitana.

Dan Lawrence is refusing to get ahead of himself as the battle for places in England’s batting order hots up.

There are three relative rookies in a revamped top six for the ongoing series against Pakistan, with the returning Lawrence joined by opener Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox.

The latter has filling in at number three in the absence of the injured Jacob Bethell, who has enough credit with the selectors to parachute back into the XI in South Africa this winter.

It is not clear how incoming head coach Stephen Fleming will resolve the situation when he finally takes charge of the team, with a host of potential solutions at play, and Lawrence has no plans on second guessing his place in the pecking order.

open image in gallery Dan Lawrence produced a fine display in difficult batting conditions (Ben Whitley/PA) ( PA Wire )

He won just three caps in four years under the Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes regime, struggling badly as an ill-fitting stopgap opener in 2024, but has looked better suited since resuming at number six. He followed a comeback knock of 51 at Headingley last week with an exuberant 50 not out in extreme seaming conditions on day three at Lord’s.

With a lead of 357 and three second-innings wickets in hand, the groundwork for a series-clinching win has already been done but Lawrence is trying not to look at the bigger picture.

“I think I got wrapped up in a lot of things when I played for England before,” he admitted.

“I was thinking about my position a lot and what I needed to do to stay in the team, instead of just actually enjoying it and realising how lucky I am to play for England. My mentality since coming back has been completely different to what it was before.

“Obviously thoughts can creep into your head and I’m desperate, along with all the other boys, to establish myself in an England shirt, which is something I haven’t quite done in my career so far.

“It’s just about trying to take every opportunity you get and really enjoy the occasion instead of feeling nervous about the occasion. Just have fun, play the cricket that’s got me here this summer.

“It’s pointless looking to the future because it hasn’t happened yet. I’m just trying to contribute every Test I can and give a good showing of myself.”

With a nod to his experimental stint at the top of the order against Sri Lanka two summers ago, he added: “It’s been great fun. I’m batting in a position that’s a little bit closer to what I’m used to and, thankfully, I contributed to the team.

open image in gallery Rain ruled for much of day three (Ben Whitley/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Last time I was play for England I was opening and I was happy to do it as a long as I was playing.”

Lawrence partially owed his recall to his improving off spin with Surrey, effectively replacing the retired Stokes as a fifth bowling option, but the success of the seam quartet means he has barely been called upon.

That is not expected to change when England begin their victory push with the ball on Sunday, a fact he is already at ease with.

“If they keep bowling like they have been I probably won’t get too many overs, but I’d love to have the chance,” he said.

“I haven’t really had the chance to show it this series but it’s another string to my bow.”

England’s lead climbed to 357 as they circled a series-clinching win in the second Rothesay Test against Pakistan, but opener Emilio Gay found himself on the wrong end of some awful luck at Lord’s.

The third morning was wiped out by rain, but the game advanced in the afternoon session, with England going from 81 for three to 177 for seven as Dan Lawrence cracked an unbeaten half-century before the weather turned once again.

In fiercely difficult batting conditions, and against opponents who have yet to breach 200 on tour, Joe Root’s side may already have more than enough to establish an unassailable 2-0 lead.

But for Gay, Saturday’s play was as much a personal battle as a collective one, and it was one the left-hander lost through no fault of his own.

Striving for a significant score to quieten some of the growing questions over his suitability for Test cricket, Gay clung gamely to his wicket on the second evening only to fall lbw to a delivery that shot through unexpectedly at shin height.

The left-hander had waited almost two-and-a-half hours after the scheduled start to resume on 30 but added just one to his total before his fifth ball from Mohammad Abbas scuttled through and left him nowhere to go but back to the pavilion.

For all the debate over Gay’s position – he now averages 23.44 in nine completed innings in an admittedly taxing summer for openers – concerns are also on the rise over the state of the surface at the home of cricket and the manner of his dismissal cannot help.

The International Cricket Council ranked the pitch as unsatisfactory for the first time against the New Zealand at the start of the summer and the battle between bat and ball has been skewed again over the past three days, with Jamie Smith’s first-innings 61 the top score on either side.

The pattern continued over the course of the 24.5 overs that were possible between showers, Pakistan seamers exacting some exaggerated movement that left wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan facing almost as tricky a task as the English batting unit.

Rizwan required treatment on a couple of occasions as he wore a handful of blows, but he remained willing to come up to the stumps to add to the pressure.

open image in gallery Emilio Gay could do little about his dismissal (Ben Whitley/PA).

He was doing so when Abbas made Harry Brook his second victim of the day, the Yorkshireman unable to leave his crease to smother the jagging delivery and instead nicking behind for 34.

Smith was next to fall foul of the 36-year-old, lobbing a gentle catch to midwicket as he tried to manufacture a stroke that was never on.

It felt slightly like a phony war, with England’s advantage a towering one in the circumstances. Lawrence, who joins Gay as part of a selection conundrum when Jacob Bethell returns to fitness, ensured it kept growing.

Reasoning that outright aggression was his best way to even the odds, he found a way to turn the heat back on a bowling unit that was having plenty its own way.

As well as six fours, he struck two big sixes, the first a magnificent flowing strike over extra-cover off Mohammad Ali and the second a sweetly-struck slog-sweep off the spin of Ali Usman.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club who have spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League.

It is their worst start to a campaign in 15 years and the summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is already drifting away, to the soundtrack of boos from their fans. This game was supposed to be a contest between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it, yet Newcastle United were the more organised and decisive side.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the Newcastle supporters, who not only delighted in their victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

News.title: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow
News.content:
Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

News.title: England light years ahead of lamentable Pakistan
News.content:
Who needs Ben Stokes? Actually, it is hard to think of any side that would need him against this Pakistan team.

After just five days of cricket, and despite their own limitations with the bat, England are on the cusp of a series victory at Lord’s with a 261-run lead and power to add thanks to the prowess of a seam attack that has emerged quickly from the shadow of its former captain.

It will take longer to feel the full effects of Stokes’s absence. When England need a spinner in the side, they will miss the seam-bowling all-rounder to balance the XI. There will be times when they are up against it on a flat deck on a boiling day and be desperate for Stokes’s sheer will to win. It is still hard to think he will not play some part in the Ashes next summer.

For the final two years of his career it was Stokes’s bowling that was top class, his batting having become ordinary. But with bowlers of the quality of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson gelling, England are more than making up for Stokes’s retirement. This bowling attack against Pakistan’s batting was a complete mismatch.

Joe Root has stepped into Stokes’s shoes confidently, laying down the law off the field and tactically he has been spot on, although Pakistan have hardly stretched him. The only stir they have made since arriving was the stink they kicked up over Sky Sports’ interview with Imran Khan’s sons.

Conclusions are impossible to draw with any confidence against such poor opponents. Sri Lanka and West Indies two years ago put up a stronger fight in the first two Tests of their series. Tamim Iqbal scored two hundreds as Bangladesh at least landed some blows in 2010. Pakistan have managed one fifty in three innings and were bowled out for 171 and 135 at Headingley and a lamentable 110 here.

They were a batsman down at Lord’s because of a calf injury to opener Imam-ul-Haq, but only reached three figures because England dropped top scorer Azan Awais on eight; he went on to score 46.

England’s batting is hardly firing, but with a 180 first-innings lead, they could afford to be 13 for two without panic spreading. Losing Root for 24 kept Pakistan interested, but Emilio Gay toughed it out in the gloom to reach stumps unbeaten on 30; England 81 for three, light years ahead in the game.

Robinson’s astonishing figures of 13-6-11-4 set him on the way for a probable third man-of-the-match award in a row and continued his unexpected resurgence. Rarely did his pace go above 78mph, he just landed the ball time and again on a length and let movement off the seam do the rest.

News.title: I’ve lived in Norfolk for more than 30 years. Here’s how to explore England’s windswept east
News.content:
Norfolk’s vast sandy beaches are its chief draw for visitors: even on the busiest summer day there is always space for games, kite-flying or a family picnic in the dunes. Boating, crabbing, digging for cockles and wading in creeks provides hours of entertainment for all.

But there’s much more to Norfolk’s coast than its beaches. It’s also a landscape of dense pine forest and large expanses of salt marsh, which flush purple with sea-lavender in August. Birdlife is astonishingly rich, and wildflowers include yellow-horned poppies and lilac-flowering sea pea.

Inland, the undulating countryside and sleepy flint-built villages are perfect for gentle cycling, walking or touring by car. Grand stately homes make enjoyable days out, and almost every village has a sublimely beautiful medieval church at its centre.

Lively Georgian towns such as Burnham Market and Holt offer quirky shopping – and, wherever you are, you’re never far from an atmospheric pamment-floored pub serving local ales, or an excellent delicatessen selling the region’s specialities. Look out for pungent cheeses, smoked fish and salt-marsh flavoured honey.

Tottenham’s squad has three Brazilians – Richarlison, Souza and new man Savio – plus Sandro Tonali and Destiny Udogie of Italy.

Sports.title: Tottenham 0 Newcastle 2: New-look Toon go third with first win of season with Spurs dead last with zero points or goals
Sports.content:
AFTER the departure of Eddie Howe and three of their best players – including Sandro Tonali – to Spurs – Newcastle fans were properly dreading the start of the season.

There had even been talk of relegation.



Yet in complete contrast, Spurs, having just avoided the drop by the skin of their teeth, had been expecting an instant change in fortunes with Roberto De Zerbi splashing out £300million-plus in new players.

There had even been talk of the top four.



Instead, with £100million midfielder Tonali suffering an absolute shocker, Spurs ended up with a result just as bad as the 3-0 loss to Brentford.

As for Newcastle, agonisingly close to beating Liverpool before conceding an injury-time penalty, they are flying. What a start for Matthias Jaissle.

And it was two players who were a disaster under Howe last term, £55million players Anthony Elanga and Yoanne Wissa, who produced moments of real class

Elanga did not score once in the Premier League since his arrival from Nottingham Forest last season but has already scored twice this season and his goal here was a beauty, even better because he turned Tonali inside out.

Wissa, who also joined for £55m from Brentford, never got going after missing three months with an injury but he also looks reborn and after an encouraging game against Liverpool, he sealed the game with an outstanding strike.

Newcastle’s fans had barely stopped celebrating when they saw that the fourth official was indicating that Tottenham’s No16 was being replaced.

Tonali, having been booed with every touch, trudged off the pitch looking embarrassed.

Throughout the game, those supporters sang ‘there’s only one greedy b******’ at the Italian, although they did the same at Alexander Isak six days earlier.

And maybe, when they are at home to Arsenal in November, they might chant the same thing at Bruno Guimaraes although he has maybe won a PR battle having written about his love for the club, even though he wanted away for the same reason as all the other players.

For De Zerbi, this was his first defeat here at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium yet things will get better. They have to.



But it will obviously take time for this huge number of new players to gel.

One of those, Omar Marmoush, having only arrived from Manchester City on Thursday, went straight into the team with fellow new boy Savio missing out with a muscle strain.

Marmoush will hope to do better than his 10 Premier League goals in his 18 months at City but he did look off the pace.

He wasted the best chance of the first as he had plenty of time to judge Andy Robertson’s far post corner but he stuck the effort half into the side-netting.

After a sluggish start, Tottenham looked better but they failed to take their chances.



Tonali attempted a shot which was so badly mishit it went across the goal to Pedro Porro whose shot was superbly blocked by Lewis Hall.

Tonali was just lucky that his shot ended up at the feet of a team-mate rather than bobbling out for a throw.

Playing on the right of midfield rather than in defence, Porro also attempted an ambitious volley which would have been an early contender for goal of the season had it been on target.

And keeper Hornicek, who has arrived from Portuguese side Braga for £25.7million, was pretty busy, keeping out efforts from Mathys Tel, Robertson and Jan Paul van Hecke.



Newcastle sorted themselves out in the second half although Marmoush had another chance for Spurs, creating something out of nothing but he could not get his shot on target.

And then it all went wrong for Spurs. And two of Newcastle’s new summer signings, Nico Gonzalez and Amar Dedic played their part.

Making his debut just a few days after signing from City for £52million, Gonzalez sprayed a long pass to right-back, who looks as though he could be a bit of a bargain following his £29.5million arrival from Benfica.

Dedic’s header was perfect but there was still plenty of work for Elanga to do but he turned Tonali brilliantly and found the net with his left-footed strike via the post.

De Zerbi made his subs including the arrival of Mohammed Kudus who appeared for the first time since January after serious quad injury in January



Yet Newcastle inflicted more pain and it was another new signing who struggled last season, Nick Woltemade, who made an impact, getting his head to Hall’s corner.

Three minutes later and Tonali was substituted for Dominic Solanke. It was a dreadful day for the £100million man – but a perfect one for Newcastle.

Sports.title: 'A joke!' - Hussain fumes as day three at Lord's abandoned amid sunshine
Sports.content:
A seething Nasser Hussain said the umpires' decision to abandon play late on day three of the second Test between England and Pakistan was "a joke".

Just 24.5 overs were possible on a gloomy Saturday due to rain and bad light, during which time England moved from their overnight 81-3 to 177-7 for a lead of 357 as they look to wrap up a series win.

There looked to be a chance of more cricket when the sun began to shine late in the evening, only for the day to be officially called off just after 6.30pm local time, prompting heavy booing from spectators.

Had the players returned to the field before 7pm, play could have been extended to 7.30pm.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Saturday's action at Lord's as Dan Lawrence scored a half-century to help England increase their lead to 357

On hearing news of the abandonment, Sky Sports expert Hussain said: "That's a joke, honestly a joke. That is an unbelievable decision, it really is.

"These fans have waited here all afternoon for it to stop raining. It is now bright, blue sky in the distance. In about five minutes, it is going to be sunny here."

Speaking moments earlier, after noticing a lack of urgency to get the game on, Hussain said: "I have no idea what's going on and I don't think the fans do.

"It's the brightest it's been for about eight hours. It's not raining - get the covers off and start playing. This is the best conditions we have had and no one is doing anything."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lawrence smoked the shot of the series so far, hitting Mohammad Ali for six over extra-cover

'Eye-catching Lawrence got his tempo right'

In the small amount of cricket the fans did see, England's Dan Lawrence clinched a sixth Test half-century with his knock of 50 not out from 66 balls including a stunning six over extra-cover that Sky Sports pundit Dinesh Karthik called "the shot of the series".

Lawrence opted to counter-attack as Pakistan's bowlers found lavish movement and the pitch offered up uneven bounce - his England team-mate Emilio Gay was trapped lbw by Mohammad Abbad from an unplayable delivery that scuttled through low.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England opener Emilio Gay was out to an unplayable delivery from Mohammad Abbas that scuttled through low

On Lawrence's innings, Hussain said: "He got his tempo right. This is not the surface to hang in on, there is a ball with your name on it - as Gay found out - so you have to score, put bowlers under pressure."

Hussain's fellow analyst Stuart Broad added: "Lawrence fought hard and played some eye-catching shots as well.

"He took his time to get in and get used to the pitch and then took it upon himself to put bowlers off their line and length, using his feet."

Sports.title: Root's dilemma: What is behind his lbw struggles?
Sports.content:
Does Joe Root have an lbw problem?

That was the debate during the rain-interrupted third day's play at Lord's, with the England captain twice succumbing leg before wicket during the second Test against Pakistan - taking his total to seven such dismissals this summer, and nine in his last 12 Test innings.

"It's fascinating that even a guy of more than 160 Tests, who averages over 50 - one of the greatest players England have ever produced - teams will still be looking at that developing trend," Sky Sports Cricket's Michael Atherton said.

Image: How wickets have fallen in Test cricket during the 2026 summer

"It also reflects how the game is changing. When we started playing, many more bowlers were looking to take the ball away and challenge your outside edge.

"You were taught that Test cricket was played around off stump, or in the channel, and that the best bowlers get the ball to move away, with your danger area the slip cordon.

"What we've seen in recent times in England is bowlers moving to the wobble seam delivery much more, looking to nip the ball back.

"The number of lbws and bowled dismissals this summer is high, and that's how teams will be looking to have a crack at Root. They'll be trying to exploit that slight area of weakness.

"There's also the added context of the wicketkeeper coming up to the stumps to the slower, medium pace bowlers like Matt Henry and Mohammad Abbas - and that is what is keeping Root more in the crease.

"You have more chance of getting that lbw when the keeper is up."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Root fell lbw again after a failed review in the evening session on day two of the second Test between England and Pakistan

Root's second-innings dismissal to Mohammad Ali came after the Pakistan pacer got one to nip and bounce away from the right-hander, beating the outside edge, the ball before.

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain believes it's a contributing factor to Root's lbw struggles, with bowlers managing to set him up with the one that shapes away.

"The moment you see the ball moving away from you, you naturally go to cover the outside edge - Root will go across with that front pad," Hussain said.

"Because the ball is doing so much this summer, any batter will go slightly across with that front leg, as they are worried about the outside edge to the one moving away.

Image: Root has been dismissed lbw seven times this summer

"But as Athers is talking about, the wobble seam then comes into it and nips back - you get four-and-a-quarter inches to cover a ball that's moving away and back in!

"It reminds me a little bit of Terry Alderman, who used to set Graham Gooch up like that: outswing, outswing, outswing, nip back. Goochy had to change his whole technique from back and across, to just back.

"If you watch Root at his best, he is a straight-line sort of batter, back and forward, he stays beside the ball.

"But because the ball is moving so much, he's trying to get across to it and that leaves him vulnerable to the lbw.

"Some of it is due to low bounce as well, especially on this ground [Lord's] - it brings the stumps and lbw into play.

"Bowlers are just holding a length, because they know they will find the stumps.

"And you have to also give the bowlers some credit. The skill we've seen from England, New Zealand, Pakistan this summer to bowl outswing and then wobble seam to bring in the lbw."

And that is Root's dilemma, Atherton added: "Nasser is right, because if Root said to himself, 'I'm going to take the lbw out of the equation and open up a bit', you then become more vulnerable to the outside edge.

"It's what makes this a fascinating game."

Sports.title: Spurs beaten again as Elanga and Wissa strike for Newcastle
Sports.content:
Tottenham have lost their first two Premier League matches and failed to score in both as rejuvenated duo Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa struck to earn Newcastle a 2-0 victory.

Spurs' big-spending summer, in which they have splashed £320m on eight new players, is yet to have an impact on Roberto De Zerbi's side, who were booed off a week on from being thrashed 3-0 at Brentford and lacked a cutting edge in their first home league game despite handing a debut to forward Omar Marmoush.

De Zerbi's other key signing, £75m winger Savio, has already been dealt an injury blow, missing out with "muscle fatigue", while midfielder Sandro Tonali, who left Newcastle in a £100m move, was mocked by his former supporters as they collected their first win.

Tottenham were the better side in the first half, with Newcastle goalkeeper Lucas Hornicek making saves from Mathys Tel and Jan Paul van Hecke, but Elanga, who struggled last season but shone last weekend with a goal against Liverpool, swivelled in the area and sent a shot off the post midway through the second half to put Newcastle ahead.

De Zerbi reacted with three substitutes, yet Spurs never looked likely to find an equaliser, and Wissa, another who disappointed under previous boss Eddie Howe, compounded their misery. Newcastle sub Nick Woltemade headed a corner into the six-yard box and Wissa, with his back to goal, hooked the ball over his head into the net.

Redknapp: Spurs lacked leaders - they must do better

Jamie Redknapp on Saturday Night Football:

"There's a lot of new players at Spurs and it's going to take time. The manager has got a jigsaw puzzle and he's got to figure out how to fit the players in, what system to use, who the best three players are in midfield.

"There are going to be teething problems.

"I also look at the senior players and players like Van de Ven didn't do enough to lead today and certainly with the goals.

"Players who have been there for a long time can do better."

Sports.title: Kolbe stars, Kolisi returns to XV as Springboks level series with New Zealand
Sports.content:
South Africa 33-26 New Zealand: Cheslin Kolbe stars with the boot as Springboks level series in Cape Town

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Greatest Rivalry second Test between South Africa and New Zealand Highlights of the Greatest Rivalry second Test between South Africa and New Zealand

South Africa roared back into Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry as returning captain Siya Kolisi marked his comeback with a try in a thrilling 33-26 victory over New Zealand in Cape Town, levelling the four-Test series at 1-1.

The sides shared seven tries, with Jesse Kriel, Damian de Allende and Kolisi crossing for the Springboks, either side of scores from Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie and Leroy Carter. But Cheslin Kolbe's 18 points from the tee ultimately proved decisive.

All Blacks captain Ardie Savea added a late fourth try for New Zealand - his 33rd in Test rugby - as the visitors finished with four tries to South Africa's three, but they were unable to overcome Kolbe's flawless accuracy.

Savea had predicted before kick-off that New Zealand would face a "wounded beast", and South Africa delivered an immediate response. Kriel crossed inside the opening two minutes, only for Roigard to hit back midway through a breathless opening quarter.

Kolbe's first penalty and de Allende's try either side of the 20-minute mark reasserted South African control. McKenzie's converted score kept the All Blacks within touching distance, but Kolisi crashed over on the stroke of half-time to send the hosts into the break with a 24-14 lead.

The 32-year-old's boot then tightened South Africa's grip after the break, with two penalties in three minutes stretching the lead beyond two scores. Carter's unconverted try briefly gave the All Blacks hope, but the wing's fourth penalty effectively settled the contest.

South Africa's Cheslin Kolbe scored four penalties and three conversions for South Africa (AP Photo/Themba Hadebe)

"We know last week we let it slip," said Kolbe, who was named player of the match. "We could feel the mood from the South Africa fans. We just wanted to do the jersey proud, our families proud.

"You need to take every point given to you. That's Test match rugby. We stuck to the plan to take the points on offer."

Savea admitted the All Blacks had paid for their slow start.

"We kind of let the Springboks get ahead in the first two minutes and we were chasing the game," said the New Zealand captain. "We stuck in there but we came up short. It's a tough pill to swallow.

"We lost the battle tonight but we haven't lost the war. We'll get back on the horse this week and go again."

The New Zealand captain also paid tribute to Pieter-Steph du Toit, who won his 100th cap, and Ox Nche, who won his 50th, for their respective milestones.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

"It's been a massive week," Kolisi said. "Last week we didn't take our opportunities but this week we did. Coach Rassie [Erasmus] always reminds us that this is not just about us, it's about all of South Africa. We knew that the mood was down this past week.

"Next week is going to be big. Some of us are playing for the first time in Soweto. It's hard playing them once. Playing them four times in a row is incredibly difficult."

Defeat would have handed South Africa successive home losses for the first time since 2015, but Erasmus' side instead travel to Johannesburg with momentum restored.

South Africa shut out pre-match disruption to level series

South Africa's head coach Rassie Erasmus was forced to make more changes in the hours leading up to the game (AP Photo/Themba Hadebe)

South Africa's preparations were anything but settled in the build-up to the game.

Erasmus made five changes to the team he had originally named, with Handre Pollard and Kurt-Lee Arendse withdrawing on Friday. That prompted the head coach to recall Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu at fly-half, just a week after dropping him, while Kolbe was brought into the starting XV on the wing.

There was another late twist an hour before kick-off when Deon Fourie, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit were promoted to the starting front row. Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche and Wilco Louw consequently dropped to the bench, with no reason given for the last-minute reshuffle.

On a more positive note, Kolisi returned to captain the side after missing the opening Test, while two-time World Rugby Player of the Year Du Toit celebrated his 100th Test cap.

South Africa skipper Siya Kolisi scored on his return to the team

New Zealand made three changes from their victory at Ellis Park, with winger Leroy Carter replacing Josh Moorby, while George Bower and Tupou Vaa'i came into the pack for Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord, who were both ruled out with concussion. Ruben Love retained the fly-half jersey, while Beauden Barrett was again left out of the matchday 23.

The All Blacks' five-try, 33-16 victory in Johannesburg had lifted them above the world champions to the top of the world rankings, giving Dave Rennie's side the early advantage in the first full Test series between the nations in three decades.

But the response South Africa demanded duly arrived in Cape Town. The Springboks levelled the series at 1-1 and extended a formidable home record that has seen them lose just one series on South African soil in the past 30 years.

The tour, billed as Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, is New Zealand's first full visit to South Africa since 1996. The All Blacks arrived in Cape Town unbeaten on the trip, having defeated the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls before narrowly escaping with victory over the Lions in a midweek clash in Johannesburg.

The series now moves to FNB Stadium for the third Test on September 5, before concluding with a historic first meeting on American soil at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium on September 12.

Sports.title: Elanga and Wissa strike as Newcastle extends Spurs’ miserable start to season
Sports.content:
If ever you wanted to understand the distinction between ‘winning the transfer market’ and winning an actual football match, then this was the game for you. Tottenham’s first home fixture of the Premier League season began with adulatory focus on all their new players. It ended in decisive defeat to Newcastle as recruit after recruit failed to make their presence pay, while Newcastle’s forgotten forwards made hay. “Tottenham Hotspur, it’s happened again,” sang the Toon Army as if it needed pointing out.

Tottenham should have taken the lead in a first half they had the better of, but they had no response to impressive second-half strikes by Anthony Elanga and Yoanne Wissa. What had looked like green shoots of positivity withered to nothing. For a Newcastle team itself a work in progress under Matthias Jaissle, this was a heartening victory achieved with many of their own additions to come in.

Rarely can there have been a club so desperate to show their fans that they have flashed the cash as Spurs this summer. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive, penned a two-page letter in the matchday programme that led on the spending and proclaimed: “We have attracted the names we wanted to attract”. Before kick-off there was a brief ceremony to welcome all eight signings to the club. “We spent and we spent, and we’ve got lots of top players,” sang the club announcer.

Time will tell on the latter point, but there was no arguing over the former. The £116m purchase Sandro Tonali started in midfield and was booed on his every touch by the Newcastle fans in a performance that only spluttered. The Italian was not the only player finding his feet either, with four other summer recruits in Roberto De Zerbi’s XI and £60m Omar Marmoush starting 24 hours after signing for the club. For Jaissle’s Newcastle, there was a debut for Nico González, signed this week for £50m from Manchester City, and another showing for new goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek and right-back Amar Dedic.

Newcastle started the brighter, with Wissa full of energy at the tip of the visitors’ attack. Spurs were sloppy and looked porous, but they did not give up a true opportunity and – as the half wore on – they took control of proceedings. On the left-hand side Mathys Tel began to combine with Andy Robertson. The midfield three of Tonali, £85m Mateus Fernandes and Rodrigo Bentancur began to interchange positions. Even the wildcard selection of Pedro Porro at right wing showed flashes of success with the Spaniard seeing his close-range shot well blocked in the 17th minute. Spurs had decent chances for both Tel and Jan Paul van Hecke too, but Hornicek did well to save both efforts.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Elanga fires home Newcastle’s opening goal. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

Something changed at half-time and the resulting shift in the dynamic of the match is likely to have been a familiar experience for Tottenham supporters. Whatever energy had been visible in the home team, whatever nascent understanding between players, fell away after the break. Newcastle were more compact, but also more assertive and began to see more of the ball. Just after the hour they took the lead from a move beautiful in its simplicity.

It began with González, 10 yards outside his box, hitting a 60-yard pass left to right and to the corner of the Tottenham area. There it was met by Dedic, who had run beyond his winger to head the ball down into the path of Elanga. The Sweden international, whose future at the club has been under scrutiny but who has begun the season in sterling form, took a touch to steady himself, spun on the ball and drove a left-foot shot inside of the far post for his second goal in two matches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The travelling support went bananas, De Zerbi looked shellshocked. The Italian went for a triple sub and the return of Mohammed Kudus after eight months out. It did not help as Spurs were soon two down. A loosely conceded corner in the 72nd minute was sent deep by Lewis Hall, where substitute Nick Woltemade was lurking in plain sight. The German held off the attentions of Destiny Udogie and headed the ball into the path of Wissa who audaciously scooped the ball over his head and past Antonin Kinsky.

There were more ecstatic celebrations from the travelling fans, who got further pleasure from cheering the substitution of Tonali. Spurs supporters, sadly, had to make do with the traditional act of booing their team at full-time.

Sports.title: Iraola’s Liverpool start slowly again but Muñoz strike denies Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
A malfunctioning electronic board will not have been on anyone’s bingo list of Liverpool complaints for the first Anfield game of Andoni Iraola’s tenure, but others sounded all too familiar. A slow start, a lack of intensity and defensive shortcomings were again evident as Liverpool salvaged a point against Nottingham Forest, while showing stronger foundations are required along with the excitement of £123m Bradley Barcola.

In front of some of the billionaires behind Liverpool, Iraola’s opening act on home soil offered more food for thought than the feast they may have been expecting. Forest were good value for the second 2-2 draw of the new Liverpool head coach’s reign and created enough clear openings to justify their frustration at the final outcome. A superb finish from Liverpool’s summer signing Víctor Muñoz cancelled out Morgan Gibbs-White’s penalty, after Alexander Isak had done the same to Dan Ndoye’s opener.

“I’ve got two emotions,” said Oliver Glasner. “I’m very proud of the performance and how many chances we created, but I’m disappointed with the result. It could and should have been a win, but after 60, 65 minutes our defending was not as clinical.”

Iraola’s irritations veered from his team’s first-half display to the bizarre situation of being unable to make a triple substitution because the assistant’s electronic board would not work. Liam Delap, Forest’s record signing who made a good impression, took a quick throw that led to the visitors’ second goal while Ryan Gravenberch, Rio Ngumoha and Kostas Tsimikas waited to come on.

Watching on from the directors’ box were Liverpool’s prospective new vice-chair Amit Bhatia and his father-in-law, the Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal. Bhatia and Mittal, who has given financial backing to 1892 Holdings acquiring a 38% stake in Liverpool, were the invited guests of John W Henry. Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin, other members of the consortium, were not in attendance. The club’s principal owner was present to witness the start of a brave new era. Turns out it looked very much like the old one, even down to Dominik Szoboszlai ending the game at right-back.

After a rousing tribute before kick-off to Kevin Keegan Liverpool were soon exposed by the pace and movement of the Forest attack. Long balls released Ndoye behind the defence twice in the opening six minutes and, while the attacking midfielder lost his footing on both occasions, Liverpool failed to deal with the source of their problems.

View image in fullscreen Víctor Muñoz marks his first league start with Liverpool’s equaliser. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Forest carried the only consistent threat in the first half with Igor Jesus, thwarted by Jérémy Jacquet’s fine intervention, Ndoye and Igor Jesus again having chances before the breakthrough. Having cleared a Forest corner, Liverpool were undone by Matz Sels’s long clearance back over their defence to Igor Jesus.

The striker, just onside, held up the goalkeeper’s delivery despite the close attentions of Jacquet and Alexis Mac Allister to find Gibbs-White, who rolled a simple pass to the unmarked Ndoye. The Switzerland international steered a precise finish low beyond Alisson’s left hand.

Anfield erupted shortly afterwards when Florian Wirtz swept a smart finish on the turn inside Sels’s right post. A much-needed goal for Liverpool and their £116m playmaker, however, was disallowed by the video assistant referee for offside against Jeremie Frimpong in the buildup.

Patience in Frimpong is in short supply at Anfield judging by the exasperation that greeted his poor crossing and defensive toils. Iraola would replace both of his full-backs before the afternoon was over.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool were indebted to Alisson for denying Forest a second goal on the stroke of half-time. Ola Aina flew past Muñoz before picking out Igor Jesus near the penalty spot. Alisson produced a superb, crucial save to turn the striker’s first-time shot on to his crossbar.

View image in fullscreen Morgan Gibbs-White restores Nottingham Forest’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

The Brazilian’s intervention assumed greater significance when Liverpool levelled on the hour. Cody Gakpo, a transfer target for Manchester City and Tottenham, gave a timely reminder of his quality when receiving Wirtz’s pass and spinning away from two defenders, Neco Williams and Murillo, in one movement. He then supplied a perfect pass across the face of the goal for Isak to tap home.

Delap’s quick-thinking caught Liverpool cold – Jacquet and Frimpong in particular – as his throw-in released Williams into the area with the defenders asleep. The former Liverpool full-back flicked a shot high and wide of the goal before being felled by the keeper, who was booked for protesting the harsh penalty decision. Gibbs-White swept an emphatic penalty kick to the keeper’s right as Alisson dived left.

Liverpool, improved by the substitutions, fought back for a second time when Wirtz pierced the defence with an excellent pass behind Murillo to Muñoz. The £34.5m summer signing from Osasuna marked his home debut with a brilliant finish off the underside of the crossbar to rescue a point for Iraola’s work in progress.

Sports.title: James Tarkowski pounces at the death as Everton deny Bournemouth win
Sports.content:
Through wind and rain, the end of summer and a new era at the Vitality. In the Europa League, Milan will visit Dorset and trips to San Sebastián, Galicia, Norway and Czechia await Bournemouth. The stadium is under renovation, towering exoskeletons waiting to be filled, new security cordons to negotiate, the team under the new management of Marco Rose.

An unbeaten home record that stretches back to 3 January sustains, though so does Bournemouth’s tendency to concede late goals. James Tarkowski’s equaliser came in injury time. Other songs remain the same. Set pieces retain huge importance in the Premier League. From an outswinging corner from Hayden Hackney, Marcus Tavernier and Ryan Christie got in a terrible tangle. Tarkowski, unmarked, stabbed home an unlikely equaliser.

“It’s not even a set-piece goal, it was just slapstick,” said Rose. If Bournemouth’s stance is that Alex Scott remains whatever the offers, his first-half goal and overall performance will only add to the cachet. In a game played at regulation Premier League 1.5x speed, while others skidded on a sodden surface, the Channel Islander made time and space bend to his will. “A top performance,” said Rose of Scott.

Everton’s situation is volatile, racked with uncertainty, insurrection bubbling. Before kick-off, the away contingent sang for the 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong, linked with a £40m move to Nottingham Forest. Should he be sold “you’re going to have a riot on your hands”, fans warned.

As if joining the protest movement, David Moyes started a player Evertonians hope does not follow the decades-long drain of young players sold. Wayne Rooney, John Stones, Francis Jeffers, the list is long. Selling Armstrong to a peer in Forest will cut yet deeper. “It would be a club decision,” said Moyes, disassociating himself from any sale, though not ruling it out. “I don’t really want to talk about it,” he said, before talking about it.

Finances and regulations dictate that every Everton player has a price, is a bargaining chip. The scorer of last season’s winning goal at Bournemouth, Jack Grealish, may return from Manchester City as part of a swap deal with Iliman Ndiaye. Such are the equations supporters must accept.

Still, Everton began confidently enough. Eight shots registered in the first 30 minutes, beginning with an attempt from Jarrad Branthwaite, another jewel, though one whose fitness record dampens interest.

When Bournemouth found their momentum, Rayan came to the fore, Vitaliy Mykolenko struggling with the Brazilian’s incursions. Scott increased in influence, socks rolled down, gliding across the turf. He was calmness personified in controlling Evanilson’s pass, dropping his shoulder and drilling his shot beyond Jordan Pickford.

View image in fullscreen The impressive Alex Scott scores just before the break to give Bournemouth the lead. Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

Moyes’s fusty reputation belies his indulgence of talent if players marry aesthetics with hard yards. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is delightful to watch, as can be Tyrique George, while Ndiaye and Armstrong also fit the School of Science ethos. Yet soccernomics, an expensive legal dispute with Burnley and squad cost ratios are likely to diminish Everton.

The manner of Scott’s goal, the defence far too open to Evanilson’s escape, offered reasons why Moyes, whatever the window brings, might soon cork the fizz. Were he able to add players, Barry clanking wide a chance laid on by Dewsbury-Hall suggested a striker would be high on his want list, despite Barry’s four goals this season.

The first half suggested Rose’s immediate influence on Bournemouth is increased directness, Evanilson chasing plenty of long balls. From the beginning of the second half, with Scott directing traffic and Adrien Truffert galloping from full-back, their interchanges frayed Everton’s resolve.

Three points should have been long secured by the time Christie and Tavernier collided. Pickford was kept very busy, he and Hackney combining to somehow deflect goal-bound efforts from Rayan and Evanilson.

“We could have scored a second goal two, three or four times and now we have to deal with a point,” said Rose. “I have to get used to the Premier League. It’s quite different. It’s always an open game.”

Moyes’s agitation was made apparent as his team ground the gears, only to feel the benefit of Bournemouth’s mishap. By then, Scott had departed to an ovation. It fell short of being a victory lap.

Sports.title: Amin Nabizada sparkles for Watford as draw puts pressure on West Ham’s Nuno
Sports.content:
When a club is an established part of English football’s upper echelons, plays its home games inside a 68,000-seater stadium, and promptly breaks the Championship transfer record following relegation from the top flight, there are expectations that naturally follow. By all accounts, West Ham were supposed to breeze through what is only meant to be a brief dalliance with a second-tier existence. To be winless three league matches into the season was inconceivable.

If the travelling contingent’s boos after this draw at Watford were fleeting, their subsequent burst of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” directed at their team’s manager left no ambiguity. No matter how embryonic this campaign is, the repeated impotency is already unacceptable, and now Nuno Espírito Santo is in the firing line.

A 46-game Championship season is long and there remains abundant time to turn things around. But when you suggest that spending £22m on Arne Engels is with a view to him playing in the Premier League – as Nuno did earlier this summer – you leave yourself little wriggle room when things do not follow the expectedly smooth course.

“We are a big club, we are favourites to go up,” said Nuno. “We have three games, we have two points. Who is happy? But me? I believe. I trust my boys. I work very hard with them. We are building a team. Things will change. I am positive.

“The fans are the most important part of our club and I respect them so much. I understand everything. I just ask again to keep believing, keep trusting us, keep going and we will try to reverse it. The win must come, hopefully on Tuesday [against fellow relegated side Wolves]. We need it.”

That this draw – which followed another against Burnley and defeat to Charlton – came against a Watford team openly treading water only emphasised West Ham’s struggles.

A side that only finished 16th last season has barely strengthened in the intervening months, with the lack of depth leaving new manager Alessio Dionisi no choice but to alter training sessions to cope with having so few first-team players at his disposal. A bench that included two goalkeepers sent a silent message to those tasked with providing Watford reinforcements in the closing days of the transfer window.

Yet after what was anticipated to be a horror start to the campaign – with fixtures against promotion favourites Southampton, Wrexham and West Ham – Dionisi’s side are unbeaten. The Italian admitted he did not know of Amin Nabizada before arriving in Hertfordshire, but few Championship followers are now unaware of the 19-year-old academy product’s unbridled talent now.

View image in fullscreen Nuno Espírito Santo is confident West Ham will quickly find their feet in the Championship. Photograph: Yui Mok/PA

The English-born Afghanistan international had never started a senior game prior to this season, but has been ever present in Dionisi’s side so far this campaign, frequently providing Watford’s most potent attacking threat. His second goal in three appearances put the hosts ahead when a neat stepover created sufficient space on the left side of the penalty area, and he delicately curled the ball over Mads Hermansen and into the top corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For all that West Ham’s vigour rose as the match wore on, they ended it with just a solitary shot on target. A hefty dose of fortune was required for their equaliser, which arrived eight minutes after Nabizada’s opener. Watford’s culprit was Kévin Keben, who attempted to shepherd the ball out of play on his own goalline, only for Valentín Castellanos to nick it off him and prod across goal where it deflected off the unfortunate Mattie Pollock and into the Watford net.

As Jarrod Bowen increasingly exerted his influence on proceedings, so Watford dropped deeper and West Ham enjoyed the type of territorial dominance expected of a side with vast Premier League experience and an England international in their ranks. But it counted for little, with Watford coming closest to a winner when Iker Bravo’s shot deflected over following a rapid counterattack.

“We will gel, we will click and we are positive that, with the quality we have, we are going to do it,” insisted Nuno. If West Ham’s travelling fans are to be believed, time might be in short supply.

Sports.title: Hull maintain flying start as Liam Millar’s winner ruins Coventry’s day
Sports.content:
Perhaps last Saturday’s triumph was not a one-off. Hull backed up a shock victory against Manchester United by maintaining their 100% start to the Premier League and condemning Coventry to successive defeats. “We’re gonna win the league,” was the glorious chant raining down from the Hull support after Liam Millar’s 82nd-minute strike.

The goal was a sucker punch for Coventry, who were pushing for a winner and looked set to claim at least their first point of the season. Frank Lampard, arms folded, was unmoved as the away end rejoiced.

He and Coventry may wonder where their first point – and, indeed, their first goal – will come from. Next is a daunting trip to Manchester City, before they host Brighton, who began the season with a 4-0 trouncing of Aston Villa. Hull, as they did last season, are exceeding all expectations.

Was losing to another promoted team, one who finished 22 points behind them last season, a mental blow? “It depends how much you want it to be,” Lampard said. “There are 36 games left; we’re two games in. It depends how you react to a defeat.”

For Coventry, as their owner and chair, Doug King, said beforehand, a first Premier League for more than 25 years was a historic day for the city. “I know how much it means to all of us,” he said, this also their first top-flight game in this stadium.

The buzz before kick-off was palpable, none more so than when King – wearing an elephant brooch on his suit, the animal that adorns Coventry’s badge and the city’s coat of arms – joined Coventry supporters in singing along to The Enemy’s We’ll Live and Die in These Towns, the club’s adopted prematch anthem. The pyrotechnics left a haze drifting across the pitch as things got under way.

At full time, it was down to Millar and Sergej Jakirovic, albeit after a little persuading, to conduct the Hull celebrations. “It gives us big confidence as a team, individuals, for me as well, because I don’t have experience at this level,” said Hull’s head coach. “We have a lot of work to do, we need to keep our feet on the ground and stay humble. We know our target: 38, 41 points? We will see.”

View image in fullscreen Liam Millar slots the ball away in the 82nd minute to win Hull the game. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Both teams lacked quality, but Coventry were undeniably the more threatening side. Taiwo Awoniyi, on his full league debut for the club, sent a weak header at Konstantinos Tzolakis and later forced the Hull goalkeeper into a smart right-hand save after Loum Tchaouna’s cross skidded off the head of Nobel Mendy. Lampard cycled through substitutions, the arrival of Gustavo Hamer, something of a hero in these parts, lifting the home crowd, but they struggled to work Tzolakis.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Millar, who arrived on the hour, had wasted Hull’s best opening with 74 minutes on the clock, Jakirovic wearing a look of disgust after the Canada winger ignored an unmarked Mohamed Belloumi to his right and sent his shot bobbling wide after a clever first-time pass by Oli McBurnie released Millar behind Bobby Thomas. Until then, their only shot on target was Mendy’s speculative shot from 30 yards.

But Millar made amends, coolly slotting past Carl Rushworth to cap a devastating counterattack. Victor Torp’s attempted cross from the left boomeranged off Lucas Gourna-Douath and into midfield, where Belloumi overpowered Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and sent Millar streaming into the opposition half with a sumptuous outside-of-the-boot pass.

“I think Millar was a bit disappointed with the first chance but then showed massive bollocks to score the second,” McBurnie said. “As a striker, it’s not the one you want when you’ve just missed a chance: you’ve got to run 40 yards and then think about your shot. You’ve got too much time to think.”

Twelve months ago, Hull were reeling from back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Bristol City and adapting to life under a transfer embargo. They made up for lost time this summer with Mohamed Ali-Cho, who made his debut late on here, and another forward, Ilyas Ansah, a £20m buy from Union Berlin, their 12th and 13th arrivals of the window respectively.

“We knew this was going to be a really tough game, in some ways even tougher than last week,” McBurnie said. “Considering we’re ‘the worst team in Premier League history’, it’s not a bad start from the boys.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: on-song Durán lifts Celtic spirits in win over Falkirk
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán, in his preferred position of centre-forward, scored both goals for Celtic in their 2-1 win over Falkirk.

The Colombian hit two striker’s goals in the opening 29 minutes and also set up several teammates for chances. Falkirk improved after the break and their ambition was rewarded by Colby Donovan’s own goal in the 72nd minute.

The win continued Celtic’s perfect start to the domestic season, but it was preceded by a display of frustration over the club’s inability to secure Champions League qualification after a four-goal aggregate lead was squandered in Thursday’s 5-1 defeat by LASK.

The Celtic ultras mocked the club board’s declaration that they aim to be “world class” in everything they do with banners listing the teams who have beaten Celtic in the Champions League qualifiers in the past 14 years, below one that read “‘world class’ embarrassment”.

View image in fullscreen Fans hold up banners with the names of teams that have eliminated Celtic from Europe. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

However, fans got behind the team throughout the afternoon and one chant of “sack the board” emanating from the standing section did not take off around the rest of Celtic Park.

Hearts held firm at the end of a gruelling week to close out an unconvincing 2-1 home win over St Johnstone and climb to second in the table. The Jambos – buoyed by their midweek Conference League playoff triumph away to Rapid Vienna – were good value for their two-goal lead after James Wilson’s early strike was followed by a second that went down as an own goal from the Saints debutant Enes Alic.

But the hosts faded after the break and they were left clinging on in the closing stages after Ruari Paton pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.

Dundee United produced a fine performance in the absence of their manager, Jim Goodwin, as they thrashed Kilmarnock 4-0 at Rugby Park. Goodwin was admitted to hospital on Thursday and the club said on Saturday morning the 44-year-old “continues to deal with an ongoing medical matter”.

His players, under the guidance of assistant Lee Sharp, did him proud as three first-half goals helped ease them to a first Premiership victory of the campaign. United, who had not scored in their previous three games in all competitions, were three up by 41 minutes thanks to Emmanuel Agyei’s opener, Zac Sapsford’s penalty and a Will Ferry beauty.

Jesse Randall added a late fourth as Killie conceded for the 13th time in three top-flight matches to remain bottom of the table without a point.
