Sports.title: Alonso gets Chelsea’s priorities right by ditching Sánchez for winner Martínez | Jacob Steinberg
Sports.content:
Carlo Cudicini was a very good goalkeeper. However, José Mourinho was ruthless when he became Chelsea manager in 2004. Very good was not good enough. Mourinho wanted the best and one of the main factors behind the Portuguese winning the Premier League during his first season in charge was the decision to replace Cudicini with Petr Cech.

There is an old line about a great goalkeeper being worth 15 points a season. It is not for nothing, for instance, that Brian Clough regarded Peter Shilton as one of his most important signings at Nottingham Forest. Shilton was key when Forest defied the odds by winning the Division One title in 1978 and there are plenty of other examples of promising teams taking the next step only after buying a top No 1.

Jürgen Klopp’s Liverpool did not become the finished article until signing Alisson in 2018, while Arsenal might not have finished top last season without David Raya’s crucial save during the 1-0 win over West Ham in May. Chelsea, though, developed a blind spot after selling Thibaut Courtois to Real Madrid eight years ago.

A host of inconsistent goalkeepers have come and gone, or in some cases stuck around long after it became clear they were not a patch on Cech and Courtois, and it is only now that Chelsea have tackled the issue head on.

The £7.5m signing of Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa adds to the sense that this will go down as the summer when BlueCo got serious. The focus on youth remains but has lowered in intensity and the decision to ditch Robert Sánchez after his clumsy performance during last Monday’s 3-2 win over Fulham shows that Xabi Alonso will not hesitate to make the big calls.

The only frustration for supporters is that it has taken this long for Chelsea to give up on Sánchez, three years after signing him from Brighton for £25m. There have been occasional challenges but none have lasted. Mauricio Pochettino switched to Djordje Petrovic midway through the 2023-24 season, only for Enzo Maresca to return to Sánchez after becoming Chelsea’s head coach in the summer of 2024.

Filip Jörgensen, signed from Villarreal as Sánchez’s deputy two years ago, then had chances to establish himself as the No 1. Jörgensen is better than Sánchez with his feet but struggled to convince. Maresca did not stick with the Dane after bringing him into the side in February 2025. The turning point in Liam Rosenior’s brief reign came when his decision to select Jörgensen over Sanchez in a Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain last season backfired so badly that Chelsea lost 5-2.

Jörgensen departed this summer and it seemed that Chelsea were going to ignore all the outsiders who insisted that Sánchez also had to go. The message was that Alonso was happy with his options in goal. Sánchez was going to remain as the No 1 and the academy graduate Teddy Sharman-Lowe was third choice, while part of the thinking behind the club’s refusal to go into the market for a new goalkeeper was their belief that Mike Penders is going to become one of the best in the world.

Penders, who made his debut in the Carabao Cup win over Luton on Thursday, joined from Genk for £17m two years ago. Chelsea’s determination not to block the 21-year-old Belgian’s pathway partly explains why they have not pursued opportunities to sign Milan’s Mike Maignan and Porto’s Diogo Costa during the past two summers.

This was supposed to be a season of gradual change. Sánchez was still first pick but was going to face healthy competition from Penders. Both were content with that situation. Ben Roberts, Chelsea’s head of goalkeeping, worked with Sánchez at Brighton and has long been one of his biggest advocates.

Yet Sánchez’s performance against Fulham forced Chelsea’s hand. It was clear that there was not going to be a title challenge unless a new goalkeeper was signed before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. The proof was overwhelming. Sánchez dribbled the ball behind for a corner at one point and was at fault for both Fulham goals. He spread anxiety, making his defenders nervous, and Alonso knew it was time to act.

Things moved quickly when Chelsea were contacted by Martínez’s representatives earlier this week. The club’s sporting leadership presented the idea to Alonso, who gave them the green light, and the transfer was completed on Thursday night.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea believe 21-year-old Mike Penders can become one of the best goalkeepers in the world. Photograph: Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

There was some doubt about whether it would be a permanent deal. Some people wondered if a loan would make more sense, ensuring this was a temporary fix rather than one to spook Penders.

More pressingly, meanwhile, there were warnings about Sánchez’s mood. There was concern over whether the 28-year-old would accept an immediate demotion. Yet Chelsea have not worried about hurt feelings. There is little time to act but Sánchez needs to leave. He will be frozen out if he stays and looks unlikely to feature when Chelsea host Brighton on Sunday. There is interest from clubs in England, Europe and Saudi Arabia.

This is life at the top. Chelsea have been decisive. Sánchez is capable of wondrous saves, can command his area and is liked in the dressing room, but he is shaky with his feet and prone to calamitous games. Chelsea needed stability. They watched Pochettino, Maresca and Rosenior change goalkeeper during the season. It is better to have a clear hierarchy from the start.

Enter Martínez, who has long been looking for a way out of Villa. He almost joined Manchester United last summer and recently appeared to be on his way to Juventus. Villa have moved on, signing Zion Suzuki. Martínez has been a great servant but wanted a new challenge. Chelsea assessed the conditions of a deal. Martínez had other offers but wanted to play for Alonso. That desire convinced Chelsea to do the deal.

It makes sense. Martínez is 34 next week and has signed on a two-year deal, with the option of an extra year. Penders has an experienced mentor. He can continue to grow and knows his time will come.

Chelsea are focused on the present. Martinez has a winning mentality – he is Argentina’s No 1 and a World Cup winner in 2022 – and has been one of the best goalkeepers in England since joining Villa from Arsenal in 2020. There is still no guarantee Chelsea will challenge Arsenal’s dominance but they surely have a better chance with Martínez in goal.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 8: Everton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 10th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

With a new manager in charge, there is fresh optimism for Everton. But nobody associated with the club will be getting carried away. Last season concluded with a respectable eighth-place finish and anything similar again would be considered a solid campaign for a team operating on a relatively small budget. The latest set of accounts showed Everton’s wage bill to be five times smaller than Chelsea’s, illustrating the financial gulf between them and those challenging at the top of the Women’s Super League.

There have been positive elements to Everton’s transfer business this summer, not least the arrivals of Jutta Rantala, Noémie Mouchon and Hannah Cain from relegated Leicester, as well as turning the Slovenia midfielder Zara Kramzar’s loan move from Roma into a permanent deal. Last season’s loan move for Hannah Blundell from Manchester United has also been converted into a permanent transfer, which was revealed in unusual circumstances, with the 32-year-old emerging from a make-shift coffin during a walkout at May’s World Sevens Football event in London.

They have a fairly kind start to the season,beginning with back-to-back matches against promoted Crystal Palace and Charlton. Their second home league fixture is against the other promoted side, Birmingham. In between there are meetings with the sides that finished 10th and 11th last season, in West Ham and Liverpool. Everton do not face any of last season’s top three teams until November. They will, therefore, be keen to make a fast start and get plenty of points onboard before a tougher-looking run of games either side of the winter break.

Off-field picture

The women’s team was sold to the men’s parent company, Roundhouse Capital Holdings, last year in a move that was understood to be largely aimed at helping ensure the men’s team’s compliance with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules (PSR). They train at the Finch Farm complex in Halewood, which they share with the men. It is one of the better-equipped facilities enjoyed by a WSL side.

The manager

Scott Phelan was formally appointed in June after a four-month spell in interim charge, taking over from the sacked Brian Sørensen. This is the 38-year-old former Everton youth midfielder’s first senior managerial job, after coaching in the club’s boys’ academy. Phelan deploys a calm, measured approach and has spoken of his pride at being given this job.

Star signing

There is a lot of excitement at Everton about the Australia forward Holly McNamara, signed from Melbourne City, where she won back-to-back Golden Boot awards in the A-League, on a free transfer. If the 23-year-old can replicate her goalscoring form in the northern hemisphere, Everton could well have a strong season and, with McNamara alongside Cain and Mouchon, they have a completely new-look attack. The England youth centre-back Hannah Silcock has also been snapped up from Liverpool, which looks like an astute piece of business.

View image in fullscreen Holly McNamara won back-to-back Golden Boots during her time at Melbourne City and has been handed the No 9 shirt at Everton. Photograph: Patrick Snow Jr/Everton FC

Stat attack

Despite having the third-fewest shots last season, Everton had the third most from Opta-defined fast breaks (counterattacks). They also scored the joint-most goals from them (four), but that can only carry them so far. Their attack in regular play needs work.

Set for a breakthrough

The England youth defender Naomi Layzell has arrived on loan from Manchester City and Everton and the Lionesses will be hoping it can be a good year for the fit-again 22-year-old. Layzell came to prominence with a goal against Barcelona in the Women’s Champions League two years ago, but has since suffered injury misfortune. There is hope at Everton that Layzell can kick on this season and show why she is potentially a future regular for England. She has previously been called up to train with the senior side.

What they say

“It’s been a tough pre-season in terms of the physical load, but that’s great preparation for the season. It’s just so important to get everyone on the same page early on” – Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan

Where are they playing their home games?

The women’s team moved to Goodison Park last summer and will continue to play all of their home games there. They made their debut at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season in a one-off appearance, losing to Manchester United, and while there is no confirmation of when they will next play at the men’s ground, it is understood that is not off the table for the new campaign.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence has gone from brink of Test team axe to a man the selectors cannot drop as stellar innings in tough conditions moves England towards victory, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Dan Lawrence began the second Test against Pakistan as the batsman most likely to make way when Jacob Bethell returns for the winter tour of South Africa, but he made impeccable use of a stop-start day at Lord’s to give the selectors pause for thought.

With only 24.5 overs possible between the showers, and conditions as helpful to seam bowling as they can be without the umpires stepping in and declaring a mismatch, Lawrence improvised his way to a half-century to cement England’s grip on both this game and the series.

When play was finally abandoned shortly after 6.30pm in the brightest conditions of the day, his unbeaten 50 had helped turn their overnight 81 for three into 177 for seven, an overall lead of 357. And with better weather forecast on Sunday, that should prove plenty as England go in search of their first series win since December 2024.

Lawrence was into the action soon after the game resumed at 2.20pm. From the day’s 10th delivery, Emilio Gay was pinned leg-before for 31 by a delivery from Mohammad Abbas that did not get above shin height – poor reward for his gutsy batting on Friday evening, and a heart-in-mouth moment for MCC officials who had spent the first two days grateful that none of the chatter had been about the pitch.

It was as bad a moment for the groundstaff as the peashooter from New Zealand’s Matt Henry that scuttled Jacob Bethell here back in June, when the Lord’s pitch was rated ‘unsatisfactory’ by the ICC.

Dan Lawrence hits a slog-sweep six off spinner Ali Usman during a thrilling innings

Mercifully, Gay’s misfortune proved a one-off, but Lawrence decided to take matters into his own hands. His first scoring shot came courtesy of a wild charge at Abbas and a thick edge over the cordon, setting the tone for an innings in which valour was the better part of discretion.

He whipped Khurram Shahzad through the leg side, pulled him for four more, then straight-drove the next delivery for another boundary. But the shot of the innings, and possibly the Test, came off Mohammad Ali. Having carved him over the slips for four, Lawrence went inside-out over extra cover for a majestic six. Later he slog-swept spinner Ali Usman into the Tavern Stand, and was soon bringing up a 64-ball half-century worth perhaps twice as much.

Events at the other end lent his counter-attack further lustre. Harry Brook was superbly caught behind for 34 by Mohammad Rizwan, standing up to Abbas, who then had Jamie Smith caught at square leg for seven.

When Mohammad Ali pinned Gus Atkinson, England were 162 for seven, though with their lead by this stage 342, and Pakistan having totalled 416 runs from three innings so far in this series, the clatter of wickets felt academic.

Mohammad Abbas celebrates the fortunate wicket of Emilio Gay, who can't believe the delivery kept so low

Lawrence’s talent has never been in doubt, though his reputation needed serious repair work after his failed stint as Zak Crawley’s replacement as opener against Sri Lanka two years ago.

‘I was happy to open last time,’ he said. ‘I’d bat anywhere for England, but I wasn’t in the best form. Thankfully I’ve come into this series with some good form behind me, and I’m desperate to establish myself in an England shirt.’

His performance here might have been in homage to Joe Root’s demand for his players to assess conditions and bat accordingly: the risks he took were calculated not brazen, and his sixth Test fifty lit up a grey day.

His fifth, last week in Leeds, left him ‘gutted’ not to have made a bigger score. If he can convert this one into a maiden hundred, the selectors may feel spoiled for choice.

Sports.title: Shocking moment shameless Liverpool fan snatches Alexander Isak's shirt from a child at Anfield
Sports.content:
A Liverpool fan has been savaged on social media after snatching Alexander Isak's shirt from a child following the Anfield club's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Goalscorer Isak was making his way towards the tunnel when he spotted a young fan in the stands. The Swede removed his shirt before offering it to the supporter. However, as he made the move to hand over the jersey, an older fan swiped the shirt from the youngster's grasp, taking Isak aback. The fan was then seen grinning widely as he made for a hasty exit while the youngster looked distraught, holding out an exasperated hand. However, onlookers lambasted the individual for the shameless act, and he was later seen giving the shirt to its intended recipient. Grown ass man tried to snatch away a shirt given by Isak to a kid...Embarrassing pic.twitter.com/0dAPD8xOWo — The Culé 🇧🇪 (@TheBelgianCule) August 29, 2026 A Liverpool fan shamelessly snatched Alexander Isak's shirt from a young supporter Liverpool striker Isak made a beeline for the youngster but the shirt was stolen away Footage of the incident has gone viral online, with rival fans offering a scathing verdict. 'Don’t these morons realize there are cameras everywhere these days?' one user said on X. 'Grown man steaming a sweaty kit off a child… should be banned from entering Anfield again,' said another. 'Glad the kid got it back, infuriating that grown men act like this.' Others credited the bystanders for intervening. 'Credit to the guys who called him out causing him to give it to the boy,' one fan said. 'Fair play to Isak for seeing that and making sure the scruff gave it back. How embarrassing…' It is not the first time an adult spectator has sought to steal prized memorabilia from a child at a sporting event. In April, Max Quinn, a baseball fan, was branded 'pathetic' after stealing a ball from an 11-year-old girl. Quinn attempted to catch a ball headed for the stands but botched his attempt, leading the ball to squirm out of his hands and bounce towards a young girl, Evelyn. She raced down the steps to try and grab it and take home a memorable souvenir, only for Quinn to fumble around on the floor alongside her and grab it before she had the chance. Earlier this year, a baseball fan was blasted online after stealing a ball from an 11-year-old girl The distraught youngster was consoled and fans swiftly turned on the adult spectator online Quinn then lifted it into the air in an embarrassing celebration before returning to his seat, leaving the girl devastated. A clip of the incident quickly went viral and caused fury on social media, with baseball fans labelling the man 'pathetic'. He later publicly apologised for his behaviour. Elsewhere, an elderly ice hockey fan was ejected from an NHL game after stealing a puck from a child. In January 2025, the man was threatened by the child's mother – who pulled her arm back, gesturing to punch him – following the heartless act. Later, an ice hockey player's girlfriend delivered a separate puck to the youngster. It was a frustrating afternoon for Liverpool fans, as Iraola's side twice went behind to Oliver Glasner's visitors – who were good value for their point at Anfield. Iraola was left aggrieved by a fourth-official fumble that cost his team a goal as they could only manage another draw in what has been a lacklustre start to the season. New signing Victor Munoz equalised after Forest had twice led through Dan Ndoye and a Morgan Gibbs-White penalty, with Isak also opening his account for the campaign. But Iraola thought the second Forest goal was unfair given he was unable to make a substitution for three minutes due to the fourth official’s electric board not working and, when the changes should have occurred, the away team took a quick throw-in that led to the penalty being awarded. ‘I will analyse the penalty, but this cannot be a professional fourth official,’ he said. ‘It cannot take… I don’t know, three minutes (for him to ready the board). We’ve already given the subs’ numbers two or three minutes before. ‘I was already angry because in the previous stoppage we couldn’t make (the triple sub), and before the throw-in I said, “OK we’ll do it now”. But I don’t know (what happened). ‘They will have to explain it, but it has taken ages to not prepare two boards.’

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola set for Liverpool medical in next 24 hours ahead of £123m move to Premier League club: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest agree £22m deal for Daniel Munoz, Leeds keen on Leipzig forward, Besiktas ask about Pape Matar Sarr, Spurs reject loan offer for centre back... and Liverpool agree deal for Bradley Barcola: WINDOW WATCH

For yesterday's developments - including Atletico setting a deadline for Julian Alvarez to decide on a move to Arsenal - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Juve throw hat into the ring for Sarr

Juventus have joined the clubs that are asking about Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr. They want a loan deal.

Monaco, Nottingham Forest and Besiktas are also in the frame.

Everton fans plea over Armstrong

Everton travelling supporters made their feelings clear on Harrison Armstrong’s potential sale to Nottingham Forest. At today's Premier League clash at Bournemouth fans in the away end repeatedly chanted: 'Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand.... If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands.'

Armstrong, 19, is a £40m target for Nottingham Forest and started the game. It is understood other clubs are interested if Everton do agree to sell.

Everton have gone back to Fulham over Kenny Tete, who turned them down to stay at Craven Cottage last year.

Harrison Armstrong in action for Everton at Bournemouth this afternoon

Munoz set for Forest in £22m deal

Daniel Munoz is set to complete a move to Nottingham Forest after the club agreed a deal in principle with Crystal Palace.

The Colombian international, a favourite of Oliver Glasner, is set to link up with his old boss at the City Ground for a fee of about £22million.

Munoz was a key player in the Glasner era at Selhurst Park, when the Eagles won three trophies. But at 30, Palace believe this is a good deal ahead of the transfer window closing on September 1.

Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool today and are keen to strengthen in midfield, with talks underway to sign Harrison Armstrong from Everton for about £40m.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also prepared to let winger Omari Hutchinson depart after leaving him out of the squad at Anfield. AC Milan have shown a strong interest in the England Under-21 international and if talks proceed smoothly, he could fly to Italy as soon as Sunday.

Discussions between the clubs have centred around an initial season-long loan deal with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met. Milan are managed by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim and have started the season with two wins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Daniel Munoz is set to move to Nottingham Forest

Gunners snap up United winger

Arsenal have announced the signing of winger James Scanlon from Manchester United. The deal is a free transfer but United retain a 50 per cent sell-on.

The 19-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at League Two side Swindon Town, where he scored his first senior club goal and helped the Robins finish ninth. However, he was viewed as having little chance of making an impact on United’s first team.

Scanlon is already a Gibraltar international, earning 24 senior caps and featuring in World Cup qualifiers and Nations League matches.

'I can’t wait to get started,' Scanlon told the club’s official website. 'I’ve been waiting to get this over the line, so I’m buzzing to be here.'

Arsenal have also agreed a deal to sign 17-year-old Georgian attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili ahead of Paris Saint-Germain.

The teenager is due to have a medical next week before joining in the New Year.

James Scanlon already has plenty of international experience with Gibraltar

United academy star heads for Rotherham loan

Manchester United academy midfielder Jayce Fitzgerald is set to join Rotherham United on loan.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 19-year-old, who has never previously been out on loan, is keen to test himself in a senior set-up after excelling at Under-21s level.

Fitzgerald will head to Rotherham, the club who helped develop fellow Manchester United youngster Dan Gore last season. Gore won their Player of the Season award.

NATHAN SALT

Jayce Fitzgerald, here in Manchester United training, is taking his first steps in senior football

Foxes on the hunt

Leicester City, who visit MK Dons in League One today, want to sign either George Dobson or Matty James from Wrexham and are asking about both midfielders.

Wrexham are still in for Leicester centre back Harry Souttar as they juggle targets.

City's Bah talks over move to Germany

Manchester City centre back Juma Bah is in talks to join Augsburg on loan.

The 20-year-old 6ft 5in defender spent last season on loan at Nice.

Leeds try Harder ahead of deadline

Leeds United maintain an interest in RB Leipzig forward Conrad Harder though they face competition for the Denmark international.

Leipzig are finalising a deal for Chelsea's Marc Guiu to increase competition for places. Leeds winger Willy Gnonto is attracting attention from Fiorentina meanwhile.

The winger has missed Leeds' first two games of the season with a hamstring injury he sustained during pre-season.

Conrad Harder is subject of interest from several clubs, including Leeds

Black Cats enquire about Malick

Sunderland have asked about Lyon winger Malick Fofana.

The 21-year-old has been discussing a move to Roma but Sunderland have made a late check as their own pursuit of a winger has hit a few bumps.

They remain in talks for Igor Paixao from Marseille and had placed an offer for Geny Catamo at Sporting Lisbon but have still to reach breakthrough.

They also enquired for Manchester City's Jack Grealish earlier this week but believe he may end up at Tottenham.

Besiktas ask about Sarr

Besiktas have asked about signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr on a permanent deal.

The Senegal international also has Monaco and Nottingham Forest offers to consider

Elliott a target for Valencia

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is being eyed by Spanish side Valencia.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, the 23-year-old has interest from a number of clubs with Lazio and Napoli among them but Valencia are hopeful they can sign the England U21 international on loan.

Liverpool have still to receive an official approach but are aware of interest.

Harvey Elliott was not part of Liverpool's squad for the clash with Nottingham Forest today

Malaga push for Everton's Aznou

Malaga are progressing in talks to sign Adam Aznou from Everton.

Aznou came on as a substitute in the 4-0 win over Preston North End in midweek but has struggled since joining from Bayern Munich.

Everton have checked on Melvin Bard at Nice, among others.

Toon press on with Pardo move

Newcastle United are continuing to discuss a move for Lille forward Mathias-Fernandez Pardo and appreciate Bilal El Khannouss at Stuttgart.

El Khannouss, formerly of Leicester, has been mentioned at Everton also as they anticipate bids for Iliman Ndiaye.

Fulham in for Vallecano defender

Fulham are trying to complete a deal for Rayo Vallecano defender Andrei Ratiu.

The Romania right-back has already approved the move but there had been interest from Nottingham Forest also. The 28-year-old can also play in midfield.

Everton have shown interest in Fulham's Timothy Castagne who has a year left in contract.

Forest in talks over £40m move for Everton teen

Nottingham Forest are continuing attempts to rebuild their midfield following Elliot Anderson’s sale.

They are speaking to Everton about a deal worth £40m for their homegrown 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Armstrong, who started against Crystal Palace last week.

They have enquired about a loan with option to buy Pape Matar Sarr from Tottenham, who also has Monaco interest.

And they are continuing talks with Corinthians for 20-year-old Brazilian Andre.

Forest are close to reaching an agreement with Crystal Palace for Daniel Munoz. Forest made a £22m bid earlier this week and negotiations are at the final stages.

Harrison Armstrong in Everton's opening game of the season against Crystal Palace

Mbaye due to undergo Villa medical

Ibrahim Mbaye is due to undergo his medical later today and complete his transfer to Aston Villa from Paris Saint-Germain over the weekend.

The contract is being finalised and the deal for the 18-year-old is worth £47m.

PSG are making up to £170m from the deals for Bradley Barcola and Mbaye.

Spurs reject loan offer for defender

Tottenham have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for Kevin Danso.

Sunderland explored the potential of taking the 27-year-old on a season loan.

Tottenham paid £21m for the defender last year

Spurs have rejected a loan offer from Sunderland for centre back Kevin Danso

Barcola set for Liverpool medical

Bradley Barcola is due on Merseyside this weekend to undergo a medical after Liverpool and Paris Saint Germain reached agreement on a £106million fee rising to £123m.

The 23-year-old France international is set sign a Liverpool contract until 2031 after the Anfield club finalised the structure of the transfer over the past 24 hours.

Liverpool are now set to pay £17m in add-ons.

Documents are still to be exchanged between the clubs and details are being arranged for Barcola to travel.

Liverpool are continuing to pursue another winger though Crystal Palace want a substantial fee for Ismaila Sarr after initial conversations last week.

Alternatives are being explored though Sarr, 28, is keen on the move. Palace have also asked about Torino's Alieu Njie and are in the throes of selling Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Clunky, disconnected Liverpool are levels below where they need to be, writes IAN LADYMAN after Reds salvaged a point against Nottingham Forest - and one defender looks like he will never make it at Anfield
Sports.content:
In the final minute of this game, with Liverpool’s need at its deepest, the Dutch midfielder Ryan Gravenberch sold the Nottingham Forest defence a lovely dummy to allow his team-mate Alexander Isak a run on goal. Unfortunately for Liverpool, Isak had bought the dummy, too, and the ball ran away to insignificance.

And that very much sums up this Liverpool team. Clunky, disconnected and, as a result, largely starved of attacking menace. So far this season, Andoni Iraola’s team have survived on moments. Four times in two games they have trailed, against Newcastle and Forest, and four times they have recovered to take two draws which have served to keep the discontent to a mere grumble in the early days of Iraola’s reign.

There are some chinks of light. Isak – with so much resting on his shoulders this season – scored a goal and so, wonderfully, did summer signing, 23-year-old Spaniard Victor Munoz. That one, with eight minutes left, was a ripper at the Kop end and came after a smart assist from Florian Wirtz. Another positive there as the German had a decent game.

Over the course of this match however, Liverpool’s enduring issues were once again laid bare. As they did at Newcastle last week, Liverpool conceded bad goals. They remain too easy to play through. Isak, despite his goal, continues to look largely disconnected from the rhythms and patterns – such as they are – of his team. His goal – side footed in from a couple of yards – may help him but he – and his team – will need much more.

Put simply, Iraola’s team continue to look two or three levels below where they need to be. Last season under Arne Slot, the 2025 Premier League champions were accused of being slow, boring and with a tendency to self-harm. To a degree they still are.

Here Forest – no strangers to winning at Anfield recently or indeed in their 1970s and 1980s glory days – found space in the Liverpool half in which to play the kind of smart and incisive football that became manager Oliver Glasner’s trademark at Crystal Palace. They were impressive but Liverpool were at times shockingly complicit too.

Victor Munoz scored his first Liverpool goal to secure a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest

Munoz struck in the closing stages with a driven effort which crashed in off the crossbar

Andoni Iraola's side have begun the season with consecutive 2-2 draws in the Premier League

New Liverpool central defender Jeremy Jacquet looks an assured footballer but Iraola’s team continues to be failed by its full-backs. One, Milos Kerkez, may yet be a Liverpool player. The other, Jeremie Frimpong, looks as though he never will. He was poor at Newcastle last week and truly pitiful here. He is a trier, but then we all know one of those don’t we?

Forest will, frankly, be disappointed not to have won. Had they done so, Liverpool could not have complained.

News of Bradley Barcola’s pending arrival had swept round Anfield before kick-off. At £123million, it feels like the kind of transfer that could go one way or the other and the truth is that Liverpool’s recent record when it comes to spending big money isn’t good. Isak and Wirtz - £225m between them – both played here with an awful lot to prove.

Liverpool do need some pace and some depth, though. The lack of both cost them dearly last season and though Munoz has given them some go-forward down the left here, there was a desperate bluntness about much of their first-half football.

There were some half chances – Munoz shot over just before half-time and Wirtz saw a header saved after rising to meet a Cody Gakpo cross. Wirtz also had a goal ruled out for offside. But there was precious little rhythm or intelligence or precision. At times, Iraola’s team resembled a group of strangers thrown together half an hour before kick-off.

Forest, on the other hand, looked well drilled and well coached and more confident in possession than maybe we would have expected given that they had lost the opening league game of Glasner’s reign at home to Leeds last weekend.

Forest have a record of doing well at Anfield and this place doesn’t scare them. Several times in the opening 20 minutes or so they worried Liverpool with the fluency and sharpness of their attacking football and when they took the lead midway through the opening half nobody inside Anfield was the slightest bit surprised.

It was a dreadful goal for Liverpool to concede, nevertheless. Newcastle cut through them from front to back to score twice on opening weekend and here the origins were to be found in a long kick downfield from Forest goalkeeper Matz Sels.

Dan Ndoye gave Nottingham Forest a first half lead with a composed finish in the box

Ndoye celebrated scoring his first Premier League goal since the opening day of last season

Alexander Isak equalised from close range following fine work from Cody Gakpo on the right

Isak opened his account for the campaign as he looks to put a nightmare debut season behind him

The Liverpool defence did manage to play a Forest forward offside but unfortunately it was the wrong one. And after Igor Jesus’s progress towards goal was halted by Alexis MacAllister, Morgan Gibbs-White picked up possession to supply Dan Ndoye and he passed the ball across Alisson and into the far corner at the Kop end with his right foot.

Ndoye had come close with a header moments before the goal while Jesus had been denied twice by blocks from Jacquet and Kerkez. Liverpool could not say they had not been warned.

Liverpool did respond with spells of possession and appeared to have equalised within a few minutes only for Frimpong to have been offside in the build up to a low shot in to the corner on the turn by Wirtz.

That was a close one and it took VAR to provide the conclusive evidence. But as Liverpool continued to play their football in a way that their ailing centre-forward Isak clearly doesn’t understand, Forest came within an Alisson fingertip of doubling their lead moments before half-time.

The Brazilian may not quite be the goalkeeper he once was but this was a magnificent save all the same. Ola Aima embarrassed Munoz at the byline to pull the ball back for Jesus and the striker’s first time shot appeared to be heading for the roof of the net before Alisson managed to divert it over with both hands.

It felt like a pivotal moment in the game and indeed it was. A two-goal deficit may have proved too much for this Liverpool team. As it was, a slow opening to the second period eventually provided Liverpool with their equaliser.

Gakpo’s turn to get rid of Forest defender Neco Williams on the edge of the penalty area was superb and his low cross found Isak lurking at the back post to slide the ball in. With half an hour yet to play, Liverpool finally had something positive to work off.

Morgan Gibbs-White restored Forest's lead from the spot, but the visitors could not hold on

Jeremie Frimpong looks like he will never make it at Liverpool with the full back struggling again

New Liverpool vice-chairman new Amir Bhatia was in attendance at Anfield on Saturday

MATCH FACTS Liverpool: (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 4 (Gravenberch 71mins 6), Jacquet 7 (Araujo 76mins 6), Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 5.5 (Tsimikas 76mins 6); Szoboszlai 6, Mac Allister 6 (Nyoni 76mins 6); Gakpo 7 (Ngumoah 71mins 5.5), Wirtz 6.5, Munoz 7; Isak 6. Goals: Gakpo 60, Munoz 82mins Booked: Wirtz, Munoz, Alisson, Araujo Manager: Andoni Iraola: 6 Nottingham Forest: (3- 4-2-1) Selz 6; Cunha 6, Milenkovic 7, Murillo 7; Aina 7 (Netz 86mins 6), Schlager 7, McAtee 6 (Hudson-Odoi 90mins 6), Williams 6; Ndoye 6.5 (Delap 65mins 6.5), Gibbs-White 7; Jesus 6.5 (Dominguez 90mins 6) Goals: Ndoye 24, Gibbs-White 70 Booked: Jesus, Aina, Manager: Oliver Glasner: 7 Referee: Sam Barrott 6

It was shame, then, that nine minutes later they were behind once again. Liam Delap – a midweek buy from Chelsea – had only been on the field a few minutes when he found the Liverpool defence asleep at a throw-in and delivered the ball into Williams’ path. The former Liverpool defender couldn’t quite lift the ball over Alisson and in at the far post but he still drew a clear foul from the goalkeeper and Gibbs-White smashed in the penalty.

Defeat would have felt catastrophic for Iraola and Liverpool, especially given the presence in the directors’ box of new vice-chairman Amir Bhatia. As it was, Liverpool’s best piece of football of the new season saved them the kind of inquest that characterised last season.

Wirtz’s ball into Munoz on the edge of the penalty area in the 83rd minute was sharp but it was the Spaniard’s turn that unlocked the door. That gave Munoz space and his rising drive crashed into the net off the underside of the bar.

The late Gravenberch/Isak cameo was indicative of a larger malaise and this is Iraola’s problem to solve. His team have come perilously close to losing both of their opening games and do not yet have his coaching fingerprints on it.

The arrival of Barcola will lend Liverpool pace and star quality. It will not solve fundamental problems that have carried over from last season to this.

Sports.title: Are you watching Joe Cole? High-flying Hull win second straight Premier League game with victory at Coventry after being written off by pundit - as jubilant fans joke about winning the title following perfect start
Sports.content:
Two games, two wins, joint-top of the Premier League with Manchester City. Not bad for a club mocked openly by Joe Cole and written off by most as relegation certainties.

Hull City famously surprised everyone by riding high in the early part of the 2008-09 season and they are threatening to do so again.

‘To say we are the worst team in Premier League history… it’s not a bad start from the boys,’ smiled forward Oli McBurnie, who was excellent.

‘Joe Cole has been a professional for however many years and knows what it’s like. I know he’s just saying it for banter and he’s probably got carried away – I’ve done it before. His photo wasn’t put up in the dressing room or anything like that!’

What a story Hull are becoming. Their colourful chairman Acun Ilicali shares transfer updates with supporters on social media and much of their XI here looked like a Championship tribute act, featuring players like Semi Ajayi, John Egan, Cody Drameh, Ryan Giles and Oli McBurnie.

But they are Premier League players, all right. Even at this early stage, Hull look more equipped for this level than Coventry, who had most of the ball but lacked the speed or guile to break their opponents down.

After losing at Arsenal on the opening day and with Manchester City to come next weekend, this was a fabulous chance for Frank Lampard’s team to put a win on the board against a team who finished 22 points below them in the Championship last season. But it was not to be as substitute Liam Millar outpaced the Coventry back line eight minutes from time to finish a swift counter-attack.

Already owner Doug King, who belted out the club’s anthem from the posh seats before kick-off, will be wondering where his club’s first win will come from.

Hull City look better equipped for the Premier League than Coventry City - Liam Millar gave them the victory on Saturday afternoon

With a trip to Manchester City next, Coventry may fear a long wait before their first win

Hull’s unlikely lads

Man of the match Ajayi was released by West Bromwich Albion in May 2025. Egan has played at this level before with Sheffield United but joined Hull in winter 2025 when on the fringes at Burnley.

Apart from half a season with Luton in 2023-24, Ryan Giles has bounced around the EFL: Hull is the eighth club he has represented after failing to make the grade at Wolves. This is the 30-year-old McBurnie’s ninth club, having joined on a free transfer a year ago. Before joining Hull four years ago, Regan Slater played for Carlisle and Scunthorpe.

While they are still likely to be battling the drop this term, they have the raw material to give them a fighting chance. McBurnie held the ball up superbly. Mohamed Belloumi is a lightweight by modern Premier League standards but he is the sort of lock-picker Coventry lacked and supplied the pass for Millar to run in for the winner.

Millar was a youth player at Liverpool and has since played for Kilmarnock, Charlton, Basel and Preston, and his future at Hull is uncertain despite his goal. He has rare pace, though, and could have scored shortly before he did, following another rapid break. ‘We knew the centre-backs struggle with balls behind them,’ said boss Sergej Jakirovic. ‘It was an excellent win, unbelievable.’

Sergej Jakirovic has done a fine job to get his Hull players up to speed with elite football

Tough autumn for Coventry

Coventry have worked hard through the summer to improve the squad while trying to keep faith with some of the players who brought them up. It did not work here, though, as Lampard acknowledged.

‘It depends how we want to react to defeat,’ said Lampard. ‘Two games gone, 36 left. We can’t expect anything in the Premier League. When we had chances to play forward, we played safe. That’s not us.’

Coventry are unlikely to face many teams here who are happy to sit deep and defend. They will play more conservatively themselves and when summer signing Sidiki Cherif is fit, they will have pace on the counter-attack themselves.

Yet when you’ve lost your first two and you’ve yet to score, none of that feels very comforting. The Sky Blues have been out of the top flight for a quarter of a century. They have their work cut out to make sure it is not just a one-year stay.

Sports.title: Marco Rose blows perfect start to his first home game with Cherries - giving cheer to Everton fans ready to 'riot' if young star Harrison Armstrong is sold: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton
Sports.content:
Marco Rose blows perfect start to his first home game with Cherries - giving cheer to Everton fans ready to 'riot' if young star Harrison Armstrong is sold: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Meet the new boss, same as the old boss. 'Welcome Marco', read the banner that Bournemouth fans unfurled before kick-off at the Vitality Stadium and Herr Rose duly delivered a performance straight out of the Cherries playbook.

Bournemouth may have a fresh face on the touchline but the football that took Andoni Iraola to Anfield is here to stay. High-pressing, high-octane and high on entertainment.

Unfortunately, that entertainment can come at a cost. And in this instance it was two points just as three looked secured.

Rose thought he was about to make the perfect first impression at the Vitality Stadium after Alex Scott stroked home what appeared to be the winner on 41 minutes. It was a clinical counter, after James Tarkowski failed to shackle Evanilson following a direct move up the pitch.

Bournemouth looked the likelier to score as the game wore on too, a brilliant save from Jordan Pickford and block from Hayden Hackney denying them a two-goal cushion.

Alex Scott opens the scoring with a cool finish from just inside the box

James Tarkowski celebrates his late equaliser as Everton salvaged a point

Everton players had earlier been furious when referee Chris Kavanagh waved away appeals for a penalty after a tangle of legs between James Hill and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall.

They were celebrating, however, after Tarkowski's stoppage-time equaliser. Several Bournemouth players failed to clear a corner, the ball fell for Tarkowski and he made amends for his earlier mistake with a low finish that beat Djordje Petrovic.

It was much-needed tonic for David Moyes, whose side's bright start to the season is in danger of being overshadowed by doubts over the future of several of his key players.

Young midfielder Harrison Armstrong is the latest to edge towards the exit door, amid interest from Nottingham Forest. That one would go down very badly with Evertonians, who chanted Armstrong's name throughout here – along with a threat to start a riot if he is sold.

With Manchester City among the clubs circling around Iliman Ndiaye, and defender Jake O'Brien said to want out, expect a busy few days at Finch Farm.

For Rose, who said he 'appreciated' his enthusiastic pre-match welcome but had to shuffle off disconsolately at full time, the perfect start on home soil slipped through his fingers.

David Moyes and Marco Rose embrace before their sides fought out a draw

Short-sighted Toffees shouldn't sanction Armstrong sale

What is the point of Everton? It's a question that has been asked a lot in recent weeks. And understandably so.

Everton are the only club in England's top four leagues not to have won a trophy, or been promoted, this century. They have finished between 13th and 17th for five seasons in a row. They last won a European knockout game when David Cameron was in his first term as prime minister.

But whatever the answer to that question may be, it almost certainly does not lie in selling Armstrong.

Despite pre-match rumours that he would be left out of Moyes' matchday squad amid interest from Forest, the midfielder started here. Armstrong was as willing a runner as ever but struggled to impose himself on the game.

To outside observers, a fee in the region of £40million for a 19-year-old who has played just 21 senior games and is yet to score a Premier League goal may seem too good to turn down.

Not so to those who have watched this England youth international develop, who have seen the maturity that belies his tender years and the mobility that has re-energised Everton's midfield in the first few weeks of this season.

But more than that, selling Armstrong to Nottingham Forest in the final few days of the transfer window would say an awful lot about where Everton stand in 2026. And none of it good.

Harrison Armstrong is subject of interest from Nottingham Forest

The Toffees have been forced to sell their finest academy products due to financial duress in recent decades. Wayne Rooney, Manchester United, fair enough. Anthony Gordon to Newcastle? Needs must.

But this feels different. This feels like the wilful flogging of an academy gem to achieve little more than a shortcut to satisfying financial rules.

And it feels like a pivotal moment in the ownership of the rarely-seen Friedkin Group, and their perception among the Everton fanbase. A fanbase who belted out: 'Don't sell Armstrong, I just don't think you understand... you're going to have a riot on your hands' from before kick-off and at full time here.

Moyes cut a frustrated figure when asked about Armstrong post-match. 'There’s been an offer,' he said. 'Apart from that I don’t think there’s much else I can say, it’s a club decision. We don’t want to lose anybody and we still need to add players to what we’ve got. I’ve been saying it for a while.'

Asked about the fans' chanting, he replied: 'I think you always have to consider supporters. There’s also times at clubs when people who are really powerful make difficult decisions. Not all decisions are popular. Sometimes they have to do it for different reasons.'

There's been little to celebrate for Everton fans in recent years, but a homegrown talent breaking through is at least cause for optimism. It would be foolish to extinguish it.

And another worrying question. If Armstrong doesn't see himself progressing at Everton, what does that say about the club's direction of travel?

Sports.title: US Open tennis stars complain about overwhelming smell of marijuana taking over the court during matches
Sports.content:
A series of big-name US Open tennis players have bemoaned the overwhelming smell of marijuana while on court at the Grand Slam tournament in New York.

The tournament's biggest stars might have thought they'd put the grass behind them when Wimbledon finished in July – but the smell of it is all around Flushing Meadows.

Marijuana is legal for adults in New York and while smoking is not allowed on site, the aroma of weed wafts over some outside courts from the nearby Corona Park.

British number one Katie Boulter told reporters on Friday: 'Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot.

'But yeah, I'm not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.

The US Open's Court 17 in New York City is notorious for often smelling heavily of marijuana

Katie Boulter is among the stars to have spoken out about the smell of weed at the tournament

'I've played on one before and I did smell it during my match. It's something that I wouldn't like to smell in the middle of my match.

'I'm trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don't want to. You don't need distractions. So yeah, I wasn't a huge fan of it.'

Fran Jones, meanwhile, recalled: 'Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round, and I said to the guy, "is this normal?". Because I was on the stadium, and it's next to the park.

'He's like, "yeah". and I was like, "well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well".

'This year I'll be like "no, lock in, lock in!"

Back in 2023, Alexander Zverev joked that Court 17 'smelled like Snoop Dogg's living room'

Back in 2023, Alexander Zverev hit the headlines when he joked that Court 17 'definitely smells like Snoop Dogg's living room', adding: 'Oh my God, it's everywhere. The whole court smells like weed.'

Harriet Dart, who came through qualifying along with Jones this year, added on Friday: 'I mean it's New York. It's New York. I feel like everywhere you walk around, it's everywhere, no? It is what it is. Same for everyone.'

The USTA said in a statement: 'While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke-free environment.'

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Barcola signing imminent, Gakpo's message to Spurs, Man Utd get Chelsea deal
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and many more

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer blog for Saturday, August 29.

Bradley Barcola's seemingly imminent transfer from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool has continued to dominate the headlines, as one of the most exciting sagas of the summer is set to come to an end. It is claimed that an agreement has been reached between the two clubs, and that the Reds will pay a total of £123million for the 23-year-old winger.

That's broken down into a guaranteed £106m, as well as £17m in add-ons. A move to Anfield is expected to be formalised in the coming days. Barcola isn't the only talent that could bolster Andoni Iraola's first-team in the coming days, however.

The Reds are also reportedly setting their sights on Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr, with Nicolo Schira claiming that an agreement in principle over a contract running to 2031 has been met between Liverpool and the player. A new bid is expected to come, after Palace rebuffed an initial offer of around £51m.

In the English capital, meanwhile, Arsenal are still chasing Julian Alvarez's signature, with his future with Atletico Madrid up in the air. The 26-year-old centre-forward has missed training thrice this week, albeit, citing illness as the reason for his absence, as the Gunners prepare to table a £130m bid to secure his signature.

Manchester United's search for a new left-back also runs on, having seemingly ditched their pursuit of Lews Hall as a result of Newcastle United refusing to sell the 21-year-old. While Alejandro Balde was considered an ideal candidate, the 22-year-old has now told Hansi Flick that he wants to fight for his place at Barcelona.

Stay tuned as we bring you all of the latest news in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola makes honest admission on Liverpool transfers after Bradley Barcola question
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola makes honest admission on Liverpool transfers after Bradley Barcola question

Liverpool are poised to announce the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and manager Andoni Iraola will be relieved when the transfer window closes

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola hasn't enjoyed the transfer window (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola admitted he is looking forward to "working with certainties" once the summer transfer window is closed and Bradley Barcola is a Liverpool player.

‌



Liverpool have agreed a deal worth £123million for the Paris Saint-Germain attacker, who will undergo a medical this weekend. After a long saga, they have agreed to pay the French side an initial fee of £106m, plus a potential £17m in add-ons.

‌



Barcola will bolster Iraola's attacking options and join Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo as the new arrivals. Liverpool have begun the season with back-to-back 2-2 draws after they were held by Nottingham Forest at Anfield on Saturday and Iraola is looking forward to Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

‌



"We've been patient all summer and now we just have to wait," he told BBC Match of the Day when asked about Barcola post-match. "We just have to wait a couple more days and see how we finish and how the squad looks in the second half of September.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Honestly, I am looking forward to having who we have and a definitive squad so we can start working with certainties."

Munoz's late strike earned Liverpool a point against Forest after Morgan Gibbs-White's penalty, Dan Ndoye's low finish and Alexander Isak's tap-in. The Reds have been far from solid in their opening two matches and still have a few days to recruit more players.

Asked in the post-match press conference whether there would be further additions before the transfer deadline, Iraola said: "I cannot tell you anything different right now. It's true that there are things going on, like is normal because we are talking about the last weeks of the market, but now we have to wait.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool are on the verge of signing Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

"I'm looking forward to having the squad [on] September 2, [so we can say] this is who we are and working with certainties. Now everything is quite like uncertain and it's the same for every team, but it's how the competition works. Now we have to wait just some [more] days and work with what we have after the market closes."

Pressed further on his squad, Iraola said: "We are talking now about the hypothesis because we don't know what's going to be the squad on September 2. I think every analysis that I can make is when I know and when everything finishes, when I know who's going to be here all the season or at least until January.

‌



"So now, we've waited all the summer, so we have to wait two, three more days, analyse and see what we have when the market closes."

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard is excited by the arrival of Barcola. "Incredible talent," he said on TNT Sports. "This is a player who has won two Champions Leagues in the last two years. I don't think he's hit his ceiling yet, still think there's potential there.

"Growth. He can evolve into an even better player which is very exciting. But it's the type of level of player that's going to help take Liverpool to the next level. So I think it's a fantastic deal."

Sports.title: Liverpool ‘don’t trust’ Alexander Isak as striker makes feelings clear on Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool ‘don’t trust’ Alexander Isak as striker makes feelings clear on Andoni Iraola

Liverpool star Alexander Isak scored his first goal of the season in the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest after a slow debut campaign and Joe Hart believes there is still an ongoing issue

View 2 Images Isak struggled in his debut campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Joe Hart claims Alexander Isak still isn’t trusted at Liverpool despite having scored his first goal of the season. The Swedish striker completed a £125million move to Anfield from Newcastle last summer.

‌



His first season was hugely disrupted by injury and he went on to score just four times across his debut campaign. Isak is already off the mark, having netted in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest.

‌



But apart from that, he looked isolated in Andoni Iraola’s system. In analysing his performance, former Manchester City star Joe Hart has claimed that Isak hasn’t quite earned the trust of his teammates yet.

‌



Speaking to BBC Sport, he said: "It is clear that Liverpool haven't worked out how to play with Alexander Isak yet. At Newcastle everything flowed through him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“That was down to a trust thing that they had built up over time - their midfield knew exactly where he was and they didn't even need to look up as he'd be there waiting.

‌



"At Liverpool that trust just isn't there at the moment - no-one is feeling it and he isn't that central point, which is leading to him looking lost and isolated."

Hart added: "Andoni Iraola has some big decisions to make. Does he base his team round him [Isak] or does he try to find a different solution within his squad? In my opinion he's got to commit to what the club have done by investing so heavily in Isak.

View 2 Images Isak netted his first goal of the season against Forest (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"There's no point signing these players if you aren't going to use them properly and play to their strengths. There's no doubting Isak's quality - they are just at a bit of a crossroads at the moment."

While Hart believes that Isak still has some work to do, the striker himself has had his say on Liverpool’s stuttering start to the season and believes they will hit top form with time.

He said: “I think there's no problem in fighting spirit and never giving up. I think we showed that last week as well. Obviously we started the game pretty bad today as well. When we gained momentum by scoring a goal, that's where we need to be better, I think, because again today we conceded quite quickly after that. But from the position we were [in], it's always good to get something out of the game."

Article continues below

He added: “It's been good [working under Iraola]. There's always time to get used to a new playing style and a new manager. But we are really working hard to try to play the game he wants us to play and I think when we start doing that better, I have no doubt that the results will come.”

Sports.title: Chaotic Liverpool come from behind twice to draw with Nottingham Forest - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Chaotic Liverpool come from behind twice to draw with Nottingham Forest - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-2 NOTTINGHAM FOREST: Victor Munoz's powerful effort in the 82nd minute sees the home side show spirit but no control in an engrossing match at Anfield

View 5 Images Victor Munoz smashed in a second equaliser for Liverpool (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Liverpool came from behind twice for the second time in a week to earn a point in an entertaining draw with Nottingham Forest which showed all the flaws Andoni Iraola needs to address. The Reds drew 2-2 against Newcastle on Sunday and followed it up with another 2-2 thanks to Victor Munoz's rocket.

‌



Dan Ndoye put Forest in front with a controlled finish into the bottom corner after Liverpool failed to deal with a long ball straight down the pitch. Florian Wirtz thought he'd equalised with a low shot on the spin, only for VAR to confirm that Jeremie Frimpong had been offside in the build-up. It was then nearly 2-0 to Forest, only for Alisson to produce a stunning save to keep out Igor Jesus.

‌



Anfield was showing plenty of frustration when, out of the blue, Alexander Isak tapped in a perfect back-post cross from Cody Gakpo on the hour-mark. The good times didn't last for the home side, with Morgan Gibbs-White making it 2-1 from the penalty spot after Alisson tripped Neco Williams following a quick throw-in.

‌



Liverpool bounced back again, however, when Munoz spun on Wirtz's line-splitting pass and smashed a powerful effort in via the underside of the crossbar. Here are the talking points.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Jacquet enters the chaos

The opening stages at Anfield saw Jeremy Jacquet at the forefront of the action. Liverpool's new centre-back started well, blocking two shots and clearing another dangerous ball, before it all went wrong.

It was the £55million signing who played Igor Jesus onside from Matz Sels's long kick. He then got attracted to the ball, leaving Ndoye free on the edge of the box, with right-back Frimpong and right winger Cody Gakpo nowhere to be seen. Wearing the No.5 shirt previously occupied by compatriot Ibrahima Konate, there were similarly chaotic vibes coming from the Liverpool defence.

View 5 Images Jeremy Jacquet couldn't prevent Dan Ndoye's goal (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

‌



Isak off the boil - then scores

This was supposed to be the season that Alexander Isak began to repay his £125million transfer fee. The 2025/26 campaign was impacted by a non-existent pre-season (of his own making) and injuries. But there are no longer any plausible excuses. It's time to deliver.

The Swede suffered a fractured ankle and fibula in December and for the first 60 minutes the worries grew over whether he will ever return to his red-hot Newcastle form. There were no promising signs initially, with Isak brushed off the ball by Jair Cunha in a 50/50 and otherwise largely anonymous, right up until Gakpo put a goal on a plate for him.

View 5 Images Alexander Isak scored a tap-in to make it 1-1 (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Glasner blueprint clear

Oliver Glasner has brought his favoured tactical system with him to Forest and their wingback-focused play was evident at Anfield. Ola Aina and Williams are well-suited to the wingback position, but it was James McAtee who caught the eye and controlled things in the middle of the pitch.

McAtee joined Forest from Manchester City last summer for a fee which could reach £30m and appears set to benefit from the departure of Elliot Anderson in the opposite direction. The diminutive midfielder is at his best with the ball at his feet and showed plenty of nice touches to claim the TNT Sports' man of the match award.

Gakpo has to stay

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo has shown his value this season already (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

‌



Gakpo has become a divisive player among Liverpool fans, but he's shown his worth already this season, rifling a long-range goal in at St James' Park last weekend before setting up the Isak goal here.

Gakpo has transfer attention from Manchester City and Tottenham and his future is up in the air ahead of the 11pm deadline on Tuesday night. Liverpool may have agreed a £123m deal for Bradley Barcola, but Munoz and Rio Ngumoha could do with keeping Gakpo as a teammate.

Iraola short of firepower

View 5 Images Morgan Gibbs-White made it 2-1 from the penalty spot (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

‌



Iraola made all five substitutions while chasing the game in the second half. On came Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas, Ryan Gravenberch, Ronald Araujo and Trey Nyoni. Hardly the cavalry: two defenders, two holding midfielders and one young winger. The changes also saw Dominik Szoboszlai shifted to right-back in a head-scratching alteration. Thankfully, Munoz's rocket spared blushes for the second straight weekend.

There is some understanding that things will take time for the former Bournemouth boss to make his mark after taking over from Arne Slot. But right now it is not looking good, with problems all over the pitch and not much time left in the transfer window to change it.

Sports.content:
Online bookmaker has licence suspended due to 'anti-money laundering failings'

The online betting firm was launched in 2021 and has been sponsoring the stable of Grade One-winning jumps trainer Fergal O'Brien

View 2 Images An online bookmaker has seen their license suspended (Image: Getty)

BresBet has had its licence suspended over 'suspected social responsibility and anti-money laundering failings.'

‌



The Gambling Commission, which regulates betting in the UK, put a notice about the enforcement on the website yesterday - and customers have been unable to access the bookmaker's page.

‌



BresBet, an online firm, launched in 2021 and has been sponsoring the stable of Grade One-winning jumps handler Fergal O'Brien, plus horse and greyhound racing.

‌



The Gambling Commission statement said: "The suspension of BresBet and Bet St George Ltd follows Commission enquiries which revealed suspected social responsibility and anti-money laundering failings.

Thirsk becomes latest track to cancel races after horse slips and unships jockey READ MORE :

Top trainer apologises for fatal road accident involving stable’s rising star jockey READ MORE :

"The Commission is now carrying out a review of both licences under section 116 of the Gambling Act 2005 and the suspension will remain in place until the Commission is satisfied the businesses are compliant.

‌



"It has been made clear to both operators that during the course of the suspension they are expected to treat consumers fairly and keep them fully informed of any developments which impact them.

"The suspension, which takes place immediately, does not prevent either operator from allowing consumers to access their accounts and withdrawing funds. Both businesses can be contacted through their websites."

View 2 Images The notice to customers on the BresBet website (Image: Bresbet.com)

Article continues below

The BresBet website says it is 'currently unavailable' and asks customers with queries to email support@bresbet.com

An announcement on X said they were working through 'a high volume' of messages, after the initial post about the suspension which read: "Important update.

"BresBet is currently temporarily unavailable following the suspension of its operating licence by the Gambling Commission. We are currently working through the matter and will provide further updates when appropriate. Please note that BresBet is not currently accepting bets."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
