Sports.title: Why McLaren thinks Norris is even better now than his F1 title-winning year
Sports.content:
Just over a month ago, it seemed pretty clear that McLaren was going to be unable to successfully defend the Formula 1 drivers’ title in 2026.

Coming into the Hungarian Grand Prix, Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli led the standings with 204 points to his name, while the papaya drivers combined couldn’t even match that tally – Lando Norris was on 103, Oscar Piastri on 92.

However, McLaren introduced a substantial upgrade package at the Hungaroring, focusing on front and rear corner bodywork as well as introducing a floor and rear wing.

The consequence was immediate: Norris won from pole and repeated the feat in Zandvoort, courtesy of a round-the-outside move on challenger Antonelli in Turn 1. He is now ‘just’ 83 points adrift of the championship lead.

The straightforward conclusion would be that McLaren’s updates simply delivered, but team principal Andrea Stella is adamant that Norris is consistently extracting the most from the MCL40 – even hinting at the Briton outperforming his machinery.

“Lando is driving and operating at a very high level, in absolute sense, in relation to a Formula 1 world champion,” Stella commented following the Dutch Grand Prix. “He's driving at the level of a world champion.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“And like I always say for Lando, what I like the most of his journey in Formula 1 is that he keeps improving. And especially after the start of the 2025 season, something clicked, which is not only a single click, but is a way of working with Lando, for Lando, and that we are adopting also on Oscar's side now in particular. And this approach has led Lando to continuous improvements.

“So it's almost like I see Lando stronger and stronger race by race. Because this weekend was nowhere near a weekend in which we could fight for the victory for granted, especially after having seen the performance in the sprint.

“But we invested in trying to understand where was the opportunity from a tyre exploitation point of view, and car improvement. Actually, both drivers improved from this point of view, but unfortunately a question mark remains as to the behaviour of the second stint of Oscar.

“So there's overall a positive trajectory for both, but at the moment Lando is capable of maximising the performance in qualifying trim. If we think the start of 2025, this had become a bit of a concern that he overcame. And then, when you have conditions in which the car slides in the race, there's not much grip, he is the master in this kind of conditions.”

Qualifying performance indeed is a key point to look at.

Over the course of the 2025 season, the McLaren drivers were evenly matched on one lap, with their qualifying head-to-head (including sprint qualifying) a perfect 15-15 split.

As F1 switched to new machinery in 2026, Norris was down 3-1 going into the unexpected April break. But since then, the reigning champion has thrashed his team-mate 12-1, with Piastri quicker in Monaco only. The average gap between them is not huge – 0.128s – but it is consistently to Norris’ advantage, amid the Australian’s latest struggles.

Lando Norris' move on Kimi Antonelli Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

Yet, Stella reckons what really has been making the difference is Norris’ enhanced state of mind, leading to perfected racecraft.

“If you want to look at Lando from another angle, I would say that definitely he is now expressing a higher level of assertiveness as he drives,” the Italian pointed out. “You know, the manoeuvre to pass Antonelli today is a really good demonstration of that. He's demonstrating more self-confidence.

“This is interesting, and I quite like it – the self-confidence sometimes is not demonstrated by being the most aggressive. Sometimes you are self-confident when you think like, ‘You know what? I'm not going to have a fight now because I may lose in this fight. It's a very long race. See you at the end of the race.’

“It's this confidence in your means, in your strength, that I quite like. Which means that sometimes you are actually the one backing off when the situation becomes too risky.

“We need to remember that in the last couple of races that he won, he didn't defend the pole position. He was actually second at the end of the first lap. But I did not hear or perceive any decay in his confidence, as to the fact that he was fast and he was just preparing his opportunity to then cash in on his competitiveness. So I think assertiveness and confidence are probably the two characteristics that he has improved the most from a non-technical, non-operational point of view.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording and Filip Cleeren

Sports.title: Norris extends McLaren contract until 2030 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has signed a new deal keeping him at McLaren until at least 2030.

The team made the announcement during McLaren’s annual factory open day for family and friends.

“McLaren is my home, and I’m very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030,” said Norris.

When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships,” he continued. “We’ve achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we’re capable of achieving it.”

Norris made his Formula 1 debut with the team in 2019 and has raced for them ever since. He scored his first grand prix victory in 2024 and won the world championship with them last year. He already hold the record for the longest F1 career spent entirely at a single team, having started 163 grands prix for them so far, 13 of which he won.

McLaren also confirmed Norris will receive one of the MCL39 chassis he raced during his championship-winning 2025 season.

Following Oscar Piastri’s new deal with the team last year, both McLaren’s drivers are contracted to drive for the team until at least 2028.

McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said he was “incredibly pleased” with Norris’s new deal. “His journey with the team is a fantastic example of our commitment to identifying, developing and supporting world-class talent, and his achievements speak for themselves.

“Together with Andrea [Stella, team princpal], Oscar and the wider team, Lando has helped drive McLaren into a new papaya era of success, helping us go from the back of the grid, to double consecutive constructors’ titles in 2024 and 2025 and our first drivers’ championship in 17 years. We are extremely excited about what lies ahead and remain fully focused on continuing to compete for wins and championships.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Reintroducing refuelling would bring more negatives than positives | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses are right to argue Mohammed Ben Sulayem’s plan to reintroduce refuelling would create more negatives than positives, says reader @Stefmeister:

I wasn’t a fan of refuelling in F1 the last time and I wouldn’t be in favour of it returning.

I just always felt that it was more detrimental to the racing and never really liked the impact it had on how the races played out or how it impacted strategies.

Refuelling was always more planned and easier to read and predict with less room to adapt and change what you were doing based on how your race was playing out or what those around you were doing. You came up with a strategy the day before, went into the first stint with say 20 laps of fuel and with little room to alter that stint length the rest of your race had to be based off that.

Before and after when it was just about tyres things are a lot more reactive, harder to plan, harder to predict and you have a lot more room to change things on the fly based off how your race and what those around you are doing.

Today you can start a race looking to stop on lap 20 but if your tyres are wearing less than expected then you have scope to go a lot longer which you don’t have with refueling because if you put 20 laps of fuel in then you can’t go much longer without doing massive fuel saving.

And drivers in general have less input with refueling because yes they can do things to save fuel but they are still limited by how much was put in the tank. With tyres they can do more to extend, They can have input on changing strategy and can ask to go long if they feel tyres are holding on et cetera…

Just overall for me refueling introduces far more negatives than positives and I’d hate to see it come back.

@Stefmeister

Sports.title: Alpine confirm Colapinto will remain alongside Gasly in 2027 line-up | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Alpine has confirmed Franco Colapinto will remain at the team next year for what will be his second full season in Formula 1.

The 23-year-old joined the team last season, replacing Jack Doohan from the seventh round of the season in Miami. He ended the season point-less as Alpine struggled throughout the year with an uncompetitive car.

He has enjoyed more success this year, his first full season as an F1 driver, taking his best result so far with sixth place in the Canadian Gerand Prix. Colapinto has scored 19 points so far, putting him 12 in the championship, two places behind team mate Pierre Gasly.

The pair will remain team mates next year. “For me, having consistency is very important,” said Alpine’s executive consultant Flavio Briatore. “We are now settled from a driver point of view and I have said many times that, while this is an important piece of the puzzle, the most significant we have to get right is designing and building a fast race car which absolutely remains our number one priority.

“We have seen Franco truly grow and mature into a great driver this year. His results in Miami and Montreal especially confirmed what I already knew: Franco belongs in Formula 1 and he belongs at this team.”

Colapinto said he is “very pleased” to renew his contract with Alpine. “I feel very happy and very settled here and it’s been even better that we have made significant progress this year compared to last.”

He made his F1 debut in 2024 at Williams, replacing Logan Sargeant after the Dutch Grand Prix. The Alpine driver is the only Argentinian to race in F1 over the last 20 years and the team arranged a show run for him in Buenos Aires in April.

Sports.title: Mercedes told Antonelli he would get F1 chance before Hamilton’s exit was announced | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli has revealed how quickly Mercedes reacted to Lewis Hamilton’s decision to leave the team at the beginning of 2024.

The world championship leader said he first learned Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff intended to promote him to the team before Hamilton’s decision to join Ferrari was announced.

Ferrari announced Hamilton would join them in February 2024. Antonelli said Mercedes told him of their decision shortly beforehand.

“It’s 2024, the year I’m turning 18, it’s February, I was in Silverstone,” he said in a recent interview for one of the team’s sponsors. “I was testing Formula 3 to learn the track, because I was going to race there with Formula 2.

“I remember at the end of the day, Toto called me over to his office. And already there, I was a bit confused, because I’m like, [this] doesn’t really happen.

“So I got into his office. Obviously, it’s Toto, there’s Rosa [Herrero Venegas, PR manager] and she’s the one helping me during race weekends.

“Toto, first of all, didn’t waste any time, went straight to the point and it was like this was even before Lewis was announced. To Ferrari. So he said, look, Lewis is going to Ferrari and we were thinking to put you in the car for next year. And I’m like, ‘whoa’.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli had won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before. “My eyes were wide open and I was like, ‘are you kidding me?’ Because I hadn’t even started F2.

“So I had still so much to prove that I could earn that spot. And Toto was already talking about it.”

Wolff asked Antonelli if he would be ready for the opportunity. “I said, yeah, I’ve got to be ready,” Antonelli recalled.

Mercedes began a programme of F1 tests for Antonelli that year, culminating in his first appearance in an official practice session at Monza. Although Antonelli crashed five laps into the session, the following day Mercedes announced he would take Hamilton’s place in 2025.

However Antonelli had already learned of Mercedes’ decision long before that weekend.

“The official announcement came just at the start of summer break. It was, I think, just the start of August, probably, first day of August. I was at home with my family, and Toto organised this call, and where there were also all the big names from Mercedes.

“There was James Allison [technical director], Gwen Lagrue, who was the one who took me in the junior programme. There was Bradley [Lord], Rosa again, there was all of the big ones. Toto in the call went straight to the point and said he’s going to be our driver for next year. And it was an incredible moment.”

Sports.title: Why F1 team bosses believe refuelling “doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has suggested reintroducing refuelling to Formula 1 as a means of making the cars run at a lower weight.

However three bosses asked about the proposal are not convinced it would improve the racing.

Racing Bulls team principal Peter Bayer, who previously worked as the FIA’s secretary general, said the idea has been studied recently and found wanting.

“When I was still working with the FIA, we had a working group with Formula 1, with Ross Brawn [former F1 sporting director] back in the days, and his team, about how to improve the entertainment, the spectacle.

“One of the big ideas of some people was refuelling. We were digging very deep into historic footage, data that we had, and it showed that other than a couple of very spectacular and dangerous images, refuelling has not done really anything for the sport because most of the overtaking suddenly took place in the pit lane. So I wouldn’t be a big fan of that because it’s proven that it actually doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle.”

Refuelling also adds complexity for fans who are trying to follow the races, said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

“I’m personally not a big fan of refuelling, really,” he said. “When I was watching from outside, refuelling, it’s just that the race was so difficult to understand as a spectator sitting on the stand.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Also in terms of qualifying, et cetera. I’m fond of a qualifying car being the lightest, the driver going for everything. So in short, I’m not fond of refuelling – and also the weight and cost and everything – I’m not a big fan.”

Williams team principal James Vowles, who previously headed Mercedes’ strategy division, pointed out that refuelling would take a lot of the intrigue away from pit stops.

“We could fundamentally predict exactly where the car is going to stop. You’re always going to take the car right to the end of its fuel load because that’s when it’s its fastest, which now means you can predict what’s going to happen, whether someone’s on a two or three or one, it doesn’t matter.

“Nowadays, with the exposure to the outside world, everyone will start getting that information. It actually takes quite a bit of the intrigue out of it for me.”

However he said he is in favour of trying to reduce the weight of the cars. “I’m completely in support of that,” he said. “I think going back to refuelling is not the right solution for it, however.

Vowles also admitted to having a personal reason to oppose refuelling. “It’s quite warm wearing a race suit when you’re on the pit wall, so I’d prefer not to do that again!”

Sports.title: Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Aloys Youmbi Decisions Sherif Musah

Aloys Youmbi returned from a year outside the ring with a 10-round decision over late replacement Sherif Musah. The cruiserweight initially struggled with the change in opponent after preparing for southpaw Mike Perez. Musah’s orthodox stance, forward pressure and clinching dragged Youmbi into an awkward inside fight, where several of his early right hands missed the target. Youmbi eventually corrected his footwork and found success with short hooks while leaving the clinches. Musah denied him the crowd-pleasing knockout, but Youmbi was never seriously troubled and controlled enough rounds to earn the decision.

Tony Curtis Defeats Imad Naseeb by Points

Tony Curtis controlled the six-rounder with his jab, hand speed and longer reach, keeping Imad Naseeb from settling into effective punching range. Naseeb tried to force his way inside but spent too much of the fight following Curtis without landing enough clean work. Curtis remained composed, dictated where the exchanges took place and collected the referee’s decision.

Frankie Wood Stops Callum Lee in Round Six

Frankie Wood broke through in the final round after Callum Lee had made him work for the victory. Lee remained competitive through much of the scheduled six-round bout, but Wood’s sustained pressure gradually wore him down. The stoppage gave Wood the most impressive result among the early undercard winners and ended Lee’s perfect record.

Sam King Outpoints Jack Swallow

Sam King used his size and steadier work rate to take a six-round points decision over Jack Swallow. The durable Swallow stayed with him and completed the distance, but King produced the cleaner boxing and controlled most of the rounds. It was a professional performance against an opponent accustomed to extending developing fighters.

Zayn Ahmed Stops Liam Fitzmaurice in Round Two

Zayn Ahmed made quick work of Liam Fitzmaurice, forcing the stoppage during the second round of their scheduled four-round bout. Ahmed took command early and did not allow Fitzmaurice’s greater professional experience to turn the contest into a prolonged affair. The result was the most predictable of the opening bouts, with Fitzmaurice suffering his 20th consecutive defeat.

Hassan Ishaq Decisions Enzo Bahiano Munoz

Hassan Ishaq had to settle for his first points victory after beginning his career with three stoppages. Enzo Bahiano Munoz absorbed Ishaq’s offense and remained in the fight through all four rounds, but offered too little in return to threaten an upset. Ishaq adjusted, boxed his way through the distance and earned a comfortable decision.

The main card begins at 7:00 p.m. BST, 2:00 p.m. ET and 11:00 a.m. PT. Itauma and Hrgovic are scheduled to make their ring walks near 10:30 p.m. BST, 5:30 p.m. ET and 2:30 p.m. PT. That time will depend on the length of the undercard fights.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Gets Bivol Route Without Elite Win
Sports.content:
Calling Wallace Whittaker’s toughest test says more about Whittaker’s matchmaking than it does about the Australian-based fighter.

Wallace’s Ranking Does All The Work

His entire professional career has taken place in Australia, and BoxRec ranks him No. 16 among light heavyweights. His best win was a split decision over Jerome Pampellone in August 2024. Since then, he has beaten Asemahle Wellem, Dylan Colin and Walter Gabriel Sequeira.

Sequeira was 28-13-2 when Wallace stopped him in April. That victory helped preserve the glossy record Matchroom can now present as Whittaker’s arrival at world level.

In practical terms, Wallace is Richard Rivera or Benjamin Gavazi with a better sanctioning body number attached. If he had built this record on British cards, he would be described as a domestic-level fighter. The IBF position does not transform him into one of the world’s leading light heavyweights.

His style also flatters Whittaker. Wallace advances in upright lines and does not apply the rough inside pressure Liam Cameron used to disrupt him. He should provide room for Whittaker to move, showboat, and fire counters at a target coming directly toward him.

Cameron made Whittaker uncomfortable by crowding him and turning the fight physical. Wallace has not shown that same ability. Matchroom found a fighter carrying a large reward while presenting fewer of the difficulties Whittaker still needs to solve.

The Dangerous Opponents Remain Elsewhere

At 29, with an Olympic silver medal and four years as a professional, Whittaker should be past opposition designed to flatter him. Rivera and Gavazi already served that purpose. Wallace brings a much greater reward without a corresponding increase in danger.

Would it really have been asking too much for Eddie Hearn to pursue Joshua Buatsi, Imam Khataev, Willy Hutchinson, Radivoje Kalajdzic or Arlen Lopez?

Lopez was the obvious choice. He defeated Whittaker in the Olympic gold medal fight, giving Matchroom a revenge story that required no promotional invention. Whittaker could have settled the biggest loss of his amateur career while proving he belongs near Bivol.

Instead, we get Wallace. Not Buatsi. Not Khataev. Not Hutchinson. Not the Cuban who denied Whittaker Olympic gold. Wallace.

The IBF created this soft route through regional belts and a split decision over Pampellone. Matchroom was happy to take it. Whittaker can reach the front of the line without defeating a single proven world-level light heavyweight.

Beating Wallace will not prepare him for Bivol’s precise jab, footwork or ability to control distance for 12 rounds. It merely moves Whittaker from favorable matchmaking into a title fight against one of the most technically complete boxers in the sport. The missing stage is the one in which he proves himself against a contender who can punish his mistakes.

Whittaker will probably knock Wallace out and be praised for another destructive performance. The result may earn him a mandatory position, but it will not answer the question his matchmaking keeps avoiding.

How good is Ben Whittaker when the opponent was not selected to lose?

Sports.title: John L. Sullivan Wins Disputed Title From Dominick McCaffrey
Sports.content:
That distinction allowed the show to proceed. It did nothing to produce an orderly championship.

Sullivan Had 40 Pounds on McCaffrey

Sullivan was 26 and weighed approximately 208 pounds. The 21-year-old McCaffrey came in near 168, leaving the smaller Pittsburgh boxer to handle a massive physical disadvantage.

McCaffrey could not trade directly with Sullivan’s heavier rushes. He used footwork, slips, and clinches to interrupt the larger man before another full attack developed. After injuring his right hand, McCaffrey relied heavily on his left and defensive positioning, turning survival into a technical exercise rather than a test of strength.

Sullivan was the recognized American bare-knuckle champion, but his preparation left him tiring as the fight progressed. McCaffrey’s camp also believed Sullivan needed a knockout within the scheduled six rounds to win. Surviving accounts differ over what the signed agreement actually required.

Sullivan supplied the heavier blows. One shot to the side of McCaffrey’s head dropped him during the middle rounds. McCaffrey later claimed he broke his right hand against Sullivan’s head in the third and completed the fight using primarily his left.

The larger man began fading late. McCaffrey pressed him and remained ready to continue. A timekeeping mistake ended the sixth after approximately one minute, prompting referee William Tate to order another round to replace the missing fight time. That explains the peculiar result listed by BoxRec: Sullivan won on points in round seven of a six-round fight.

A Championship Born Under Protest

Tate awarded Sullivan the decision based on the greater number of clean blows. McCaffrey’s camp protested, maintaining that lasting six rounds entitled him to a draw. The absence of an athletic commission left no independent authority to settle the disagreement. The promoter controlled the money, the referee’s interpretation determined the result, and McCaffrey’s only remaining option was a lawsuit.

The crowd treated McCaffrey’s survival as a moral triumph. Sullivan still collected nearly $6,000, representing approximately 60 percent of the gate, while McCaffrey received far less.

Sullivan became recognized as boxing’s first gloved heavyweight champion, yet the sport had not suddenly become modern merely because the fighters wore gloves. The disputed terms, confused timekeeping and uncertain ruling showed that Queensberry rules had arrived before boxing possessed a reliable system for enforcing them.

Sullivan later retained his bare-knuckle claim by defeating Jake Kilrain over 75 rounds in 1889. James J. Corbett finally took the gloved championship from him in 1892. McCaffrey continued boxing larger opponents, later becoming an instructor and police officer while insisting for the rest of his life that Sullivan had never properly beaten him.

Chester Park in Cincinnati, photographed in 1911. John L. Sullivan fought Dominick McCaffrey at the venue in 1885. Photo: Columbus Metropolitan Library/DPLA, public domain.

Sports.title: Healthy Hrgovic Ready To Test Itauma’s Experience
Sports.content:
Sanchez is not designing the strategy around landing one perfect heavyweight punch. He wants Hrgovic to force Itauma into situations the 21-year-old has avoided during a carefully controlled climb through the division. Itauma’s lack of professional rounds gives Hrgovic an area to attack. The young southpaw has usually removed opponents before a fight develops, while Hrgovic completed 12 physical rounds with Zhang.

If Hrgovic absorbs the initial assault, Itauma must handle his pace and maintain his speed against a heavyweight who will continue forcing exchanges. The Croatian’s right hand also provides a direct weapon against Itauma’s southpaw stance. Itauma has shown a tendency to retreat in straight lines when opponents reach him, leaving room for Hrgovic’s straight right or the heavier shot over the lead shoulder. Itauma’s hand speed may let him control the early exchanges, but pulling back with his head upright becomes more dangerous against a puncher of Hrgovic’s size.

Before turning professional, Itauma had limited amateur experience. Sanchez described his previous opposition as “selected opponents” and called Hrgovic his first top 5 or top 10 heavyweight.

Sanchez believes the hype machine crowned Itauma before he deserved it, giving Hrgovic every reason to ruin the party. The plan does not involve giving away early rounds while waiting for the youngster to fade. He wants Hrgovic taking the fight to Itauma from the first bell.

Itauma has never shared the ring with someone carrying Hrgovic’s physical size, battle-tested chin, or professional pedigree. If the quick stoppage eludes him, the young prospect will have to demonstrate real staying power against a foe who stands his ground.

Moses Itauma Shoves Hrgovic Off Weigh-In Stage

Moses Itauma initiated an ugly weigh-in clash today by shoving Filip Hrgovic backward and off the stage before their vacant IBF heavyweight title fight at London’s O2 Arena.

After regaining his balance, Hrgovic stepped forward and slapped Itauma across the face with his right hand. Itauma tried to reach the Croatian heavyweight, but security and members of both teams held the fighters apart.

Itauma started it by pushing Hrgovic off the edge of an elevated stage, where a bad landing carried more danger than anything likely to happen during a standard staredown. He was upset about Hrgovic stepping in front of him, partially for a double-biceps pose. It was pretty harmless stuff, but Itauma got heated enough to shove Hrgovic while his back was turned.

Hrgovic Exposes Itauma’s Temper

Hrgovic repeatedly labeled Itauma a protected “golden child” steered carefully toward this title opportunity. The way that Itauma lost his temper today was a signal that Hrgovic’s comments have gotten to him.

The reaction exposes genuine vulnerability. Confident fighters shrug off verbal insults, flash a grin, and settle business inside the ropes. Instead, the 21-year-old met a standard pose with physical aggression, proving his patience snaps the moment he feels slighted.

Hrgovic now holds a clear psychological target. If he roughs up Itauma on the inside, leans hard during clinches, and turns early rounds into a grueling dogfight, the young puncher must avoid unraveling into reckless mistakes.

Itauma hit the scale at 241.7 pounds, while Hrgovic came in trim at 236.2. The scale numbers do not dictate tactics outright, but the Croatian’s lean conditioning favors an active plan built on movement, straight right hands through the southpaw guard, and non-stop pressure.

Itauma has not faced incoming fire from anyone carrying Hrgovic’s rare blend of size, physical power, and battle-tested experience. The opposition fed to the young prospect so far sits firmly in the journeyman category, save for a 38-year-old, faded Dillian Whyte.

Hrgovic has already faced monstrous punchers, absorbing full-force bombs from Zhilei Zhang and trading heavy artillery with Daniel Dubois. Shoving someone off an elevated stage is simple. Keeping composure once Hrgovic connects with clean right hands will prove whether Itauma is truly ready for the elite level.

Sports.title: Benn’s Lack Of Real Power Spells Trouble Against Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Benn has not stopped an opponent since his second-round win over Chris van Heerden in April 2022. His five subsequent fights have covered 56 rounds, producing four decision wins and one decision loss. He dropped Chris Eubank Jr twice in the final round of their rematch, showing that he can hurt an opponent, but the fight still reached the scorecards.

That record supports Malignaggi’s boxing argument without proving anything about the testing case. Benn carries enough power to get an opponent’s attention, but Malignaggi does not consider it heavy enough to compensate for the difference in skill or prevent Garcia from waiting on the counter.

Benn Must Survive Garcia’s First Counter

Benn’s usual pressure may bring him directly into Garcia’s most dangerous punch. He tends to attack in straight lines and does not always disguise his entry with feints, head movement, or a jab. Garcia needs only a small opening to release the left hook while Benn is stepping toward him.

Such a punch is harder to see than a hook thrown during a stationary exchange. Benn will be moving into its force, increasing the damage while reducing his time to react. Malignaggi does not expect Garcia to overwhelm him with a long combination. He sees one fast counter changing the fight.

Returning to 147 pounds adds another concern. Benn has not made the welterweight limit since 2022. He boxed Chris Eubank Jr twice near the middleweight limit and weighed 149½ pounds against Regis Prograis in April. Those extra 2½ pounds do not sound substantial, but removing them after several years at higher weights may affect his stamina, reactions and ability to absorb Garcia’s counters.

A change in approach can make the entry less predictable. Feints and lateral steps would make it harder for Garcia to time the left hook. Repeating the same straight attack gives the faster puncher a clear target.

Ryan also creates opportunities once the distance closes. He often retreats in straight lines with his chin raised when placed under pressure. If Benn can reach his chest without absorbing the first counter, he can drive Ryan toward the ropes and force him to fight at close range.

Close quarters favor Benn’s physical style. He can attack the body, use his shoulders, and keep Garcia from setting his feet. Garcia’s defense becomes less reliable when an opponent prevents him from controlling the punching distance.

The difficulty is getting inside repeatedly. Garcia had roughly 200 amateur fights, while Benn’s amateur career consisted of only about 20. That difference gave Garcia far more time to learn distance, rhythm and shot selection before turning professional. Benn has gained experience during his professional career, but adjustments under pressure may still favor the fighter with the deeper foundation.

Targeting the body may help take some speed from Ryan. Benn will need patience rather than immediately reaching for the head once exchanges begin. Reckless pressure gives Garcia exactly the rhythm Malignaggi believes will produce the knockout.

Motivation and concentration remain the qualification in Malignaggi’s pick. Garcia has delivered different versions of himself based on his preparation and mental state. The focused version possesses enough speed, timing and power to expose Benn’s defensive openings.

Surviving the initial counters would make the contest more favorable to Benn. Ryan can lose discipline over 12 rounds, tire from repeatedly loading up and grow frustrated when an opponent refuses to break. Benn’s work rate and physical pressure then become more valuable during the later rounds.

Toughness alone will not protect Benn during the first exchanges. Garcia does not have to be the busier fighter or hold his ground for the full distance. One repeated aggressive entry may be enough to bring the counter Malignaggi expects.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Picks Mbilli To Overwhelm Canelo
Sports.content:
“I get the competitiveness of Canelo, and I respect it because lately I haven’t really respected a lot of his opponent choices. I respect the move that he’s making, but it’s a tough fight, and at 36, that kind of pace, I don’t think it’s something he can handle.” “I don’t think Canelo beats him. Pace is the worst thing for Canelo. I think Canelo is more skilled than Mbilli, but when you couldn’t handle a fast pace in your prime, a fast pace like that at 36 years old is tough. Mbilli makes up for his lack of skills with his pace. He’s not here because of his skills. I don’t know if Canelo can offset that pace. I really don’t,” said Malignaggi to Fight Hub TV.

The age difference alone does not decide the fight. What favors Mbilli is his willingness to keep working after the first combination. Alvarez has become increasingly selective with his punches, conserving energy and waiting for clean counters instead of matching an opponent’s activity.

Canelo’s Guard Will Absorb More Than Punches

A high guard allows Alvarez to catch punches on his gloves, shoulders and forearms. That defense limits clean contact, but it does not remove the physical cost of blocking repeated combinations. Dmitry Bivol kept hitting the guard and forced Alvarez to carry the weight of his attacks.

Not every punch must reach Canelo’s head or body. Blows landing on the arms can gradually reduce the speed and authority of Alvarez’s counters. If his shoulders and biceps begin to tire by the middle rounds, the technical advantage Malignaggi identified becomes harder to use.

Portions of recent fights have also found Canelo along the ropes, reducing his movement and looking for single counters. Resting there is far more dangerous against Mbilli. The challenger works at close range without waiting to see the effect of every shot. Even blocked combinations can leave an impression with judges if Alvarez remains covered while Mbilli controls the action.

The difference in activity was visible on the same September 2025 card. Mbilli threw 787 punches across 10 rounds against Lester Martinez, nearly 79 per round. Canelo attempted only 338 during his 12-round loss to Terence Crawford, an average of just over 28. Mbilli threw 449 more punches despite boxing six fewer minutes. The figures come from unofficial CompuBox totals published by The Ring and Sports Illustrated.

That output came despite Martinez repeatedly shoving Mbilli backward to create separation before punching. Those interruptions kept Mbilli from remaining at the distance where he did his best work. Canelo is unlikely to match that activity or spend the fight continually pushing Mbilli outside.

Alvarez landed 83 of 260 power punches against Crawford but attempted only 78 jabs. Those figures show how dependent he has become on selective power shots rather than sustained combinations. Mbilli will give him far less recovery time between those attempts.

Early body work offers Canelo his best chance to reduce that output. He cannot afford to wait several rounds before targeting the ribs and liver. Mbilli must be given a reason to slow down before his pressure begins draining Alvarez’s arms and legs.

The opportunity will be there because Mbilli can be hit. He leans over his front foot while unloading, leaving a lane for Canelo’s right uppercut and short hooks. Sergiy Derevyanchenko found Mbilli’s chin with counters despite fighting with an injured arm. Alvarez is more accurate and carries considerably more power.

The fight therefore turns on one question. Can Canelo hurt Mbilli badly enough early to control the pace, or can Mbilli absorb those counters and continue throwing?

Scorecard interpretation adds another difficulty. Judges often favor Canelo’s clean, visible counters over punches caught on his guard. Mbilli cannot depend on activity alone. He must keep Alvarez defending long enough to make control of each round unmistakable.

Respect for Canelo’s decision to accept the fight does not erase the physical concern. Alvarez may be the more complete boxer, but Mbilli owns the weapon Malignaggi believes Canelo is least equipped to handle at this stage of his career.

Sports.title: IBF Tries To End Jai Opetaia Lawsuit Early
Sports.content:
It argues that its rules required Opetaia to bring the case in New Jersey, where the IBF is based. The organization also claims he went to court without completing its mandatory internal appeal process. Opetaia has until September 8 to respond.

Those objections give the IBF a chance to attack the lawsuit without immediately defending the decision to remove Opetaia as cruiserweight champion. A ruling based on venue or internal appeal grounds would not establish that his accusations lack merit.

He may be allowed to refile in New Jersey or complete the IBF appeal procedure before returning to court. A dismissal with prejudice would cause far greater damage by preventing him from bringing the same claims again.

The $73,000 Sanctioning Fee

The complaint alleges that the IBF accepted Opetaia’s $73,000 sanctioning fee shortly before his March 8 fight with Brandon Glanton, then withdrew approval for the contest. The organization says the payment arrived March 6 and was returned the next day.

The timing is central to Opetaia’s claim under the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act. His complaint accuses the IBF of accepting the money without making required disclosures to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

The IBF says it withdrew sanction after learning that the Zuffa Boxing cruiserweight title would be awarded. Its rules recognize unifications involving only the IBF, WBA, WBC, and WBO.

His lawsuit argues that the refusal to recognize Zuffa’s title was part of coordinated action intended to punish him for joining a competing boxing operation. The accusation has not been proven, but it places the control exercised by boxing’s four established sanctioning bodies at the center of the case.

Mikaelian Risks His WBC Championship

Noel Mikaelian is now testing that control from another direction. The WBC ordered him to defend against David Benavidez, but Mikaelian accepted a September 12 fight with Opetaia instead.

Desai said Mikaelian is expected to be stripped, although the WBC has not issued a final ruling. The reason would be his failure to make the ordered Benavidez defense, not his participation in a Zuffa Boxing event.

His choice also shows the limits of sanctioning body authority. Opetaia remains The Ring champion and the leading cruiserweight despite losing the IBF belt. Mikaelian evidently considers facing him on the Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn card valuable enough to risk his own championship.

The IBF and WBC can remove their belts. They cannot make Opetaia less formidable or prevent the division’s leading fighters from treating him as its central figure.

Sports.title: Who’s who in the Tszyu Zoo
Sports.content:
In 2020, Tszyu had the first key fight of his career, facing fellow Australian and former world champion, Jeff Horn. Tszyu battered the former champion using his jab, uppercuts and big right hands to the body and head, hurting him and breaking him down to force a retirement TKO in the eighth round.

Tszyu’s next key fight was against the durable and courageous Japanese fighter, Takeshi Inoue, in November 2021.

This was Tszyu’s 20th fight of his career, and this fight proved to be a turning point for him as a fighter on the international stage. Although he was outgunned, Inoue fought with passion and pride to give Tszyu a hard fight and take Tszyu the twelve-round distance for the first time.

In March, 2024, Tszyu, on late notice, traveled to Las Vegas to face the towering junior middleweight champion, Sebastian Fundora, in what was an iconic fight for both boxers. Both fighters, splattered in blood and both hurt by accident and intention, gave the fans a fight to remember, with Fundora winning by a split decision. Inexperience and a stubborn refusal to accept defeat cost him the fight.

Another key fight was his fight against the Chechen come-forward fighter, Bakhram Murtazaliev in October 2024, just six months after recovering and healing from a bad cut to the top of his head in the Fundora fight.

Tszyu was battered into a state of shock and disbelief, then knocked down numerous times until the fight was stopped in the third round in Orlando, Florida.

Tszyu returned to Sydney and back to the drawing board . Six months later, he took a confidence-building fight against the unrated and limited fighter Joey Spencer, to then go back three months later to face Sebastian Fundora for the WBC light middleweight championship of the world.

In the return match, Fundora fought smart, outboxing Tszyu by using his skill , timing, and natural ability, beating the Australian to force a corner retirement at the end of the 7th round.

Tszyu came back in December, beating unknown Anthony Velasquez in Sydney.

After beating Denis Nurja in April 2026, Tszyu focused on the Spence Jnr fight, and the win was deemed by many as a tremendous victory. My view on this is yes, it was good to have the name of Errol Spence Jnr on his record, but the key factor in the decision win was that it has kept his career alive.

So where does he go from here? With a new management and coaching team around him, as well as fighting at his new weight of 160 pounds, what’s next?

Erislandy Lara is the WBA middleweight champion. With a good record of 32 wins ( 19 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the Cuban southpaw is 43 years old, and since 2022, he has battered Gary ‘Spike’ O’Sullivan, destroyed Michael Zerafa, proved to be too much for Danny Garcia, and in December 2025, he beat Johan Gonzales on points. Lara has not fought in 2026. On any given night, a motivated Lara is and can be an awkward and dangerous opponent for anyone.

Carlos Adames is the WBC middleweight champion. The Dominican Republic puncher has a great record with 25 ( 18 KOs) and 1 defeat. He is 32 years old, and he consistently fights only once a year.

Aaron McKenna is the IBF middleweight champion. The newly crowned Irishman is 27 years old, and he is an unbeaten, well-schooled boxer . His record stands at 21-0. ( 10 KOs) McKenna is 6’3, and he has a 75-inch reach. He won the World title, beating the Italian Etinosa Oliha in early August, and prior to that he outboxed the experienced Liam Smith. He has a tremendous work rate, and he has speed.

Denzel Bentley. WBO middleweight champion. With a record of 22 wins ( 18 KOs), 3 losses, and 1 draw, the 31-year-old Englishman was the interim champion, to then be elevated to the WBO champion due to Janibek Alimkhanuly relinquishing his title to move up to super middleweight.

My view is, all roads lead to Jermell Charlo. He could be the path of least resistance for a big money fight. He is still a name, and he was the junior middleweight champion of the world. He has been inactive since being outboxed and outmuscled by Saul Canelo Alvarez in September 2023. He has a record of 35-2-1 with 19 KOs. He would be moving up in weight to meet Tszyu, and that would suit the 36-year-old at this stage of his career. If staged in Australia, the fight will sell as there has been some history of trash talking by both fighters, and for Tszyu, this could be his swan song, so it makes great business sense for him and also lucrative for Charlo.

The question is, will Tszyu wait and fight for a mandatory shot at one of the world champions, or will he make a move on Charlo?

Gary Todd is an international best-selling author, and he has been involved in all aspects of the sport of boxing for decades . Check out his latest book, “ Greatest Ever Boxing Champions. Their mindset. Their Workouts, Their Journeys.”

Ghana News.title: Rotary Club of Accra-Airport, SCEF donate school supplies to over 200 street-connected children
Ghana News.content:
Rotary Club of Accra-Airport, in partnership with the Street Children Empowerment Foundation (SCEF), has donated back-to-school items to more than 200 street-connected children in the Accra Metropolitan Area as part of efforts to support their education and secure a better future.

The beneficiaries received the items at a back-to-school programme held at the Wesley Methodist Basic School in Accra on Saturday, August 29, 2026. The items include: Exercise Books, Note Books, Pens, Pencils, Erasers, Rulers and other educational materials.

The initiative, under the theme: “Quality Education: The Pathway to a Brighter Future,” brought together representatives of SCEF, Rotarians, beneficiaries and other stakeholders to encourage vulnerable children to remain committed to their education.

President of the Rotary Club of Accra-Airport, Rotarian David Kwatia Nyante, said education remained a powerful tool for transforming lives, restoring dignity and creating opportunities for children.

He said the Rotary Club's partnership with SCEF had over the years focused on supporting vulnerable children, particularly those connected to the streets, by helping to provide them with opportunities to pursue their education.

“Education is far more than lessons in a classroom, it’s a powerful force that transforms lives, restores dignity, opens doors, and creates lasting opportunities,” he said.

Mr. Nyante stressed that the provision of school supplies was aimed at ensuring that children did not miss out on learning because they lacked basic educational materials. He noted that the impact of the intervention could be seen in the stories of beneficiaries who had returned to school with renewed confidence and hope for the future.

“Education empowers, builds confidence, strengthens communities, and equips children with the knowledge and values to shape their own futures,” he added.

“To our dear beneficiaries, I urge you to take your education seriously. Your current circumstances do not define your future,” he said, urging them to remain disciplined and determined in pursuing their dreams.

The Rotary Club of Accra-Airport President further appealed to corporate organizations, community leaders, civil society organizations and individuals to support initiatives aimed at helping vulnerable children stay in school. He said, supporting through funding, school supplies, mentorship, and skills training and volunteering could help create more opportunities for children and ensure that no child was left behind because of hardship or a lack of opportunity.

Founder and Executive Director of SCEF, Paul Semeh, also addressed the gathering, highlighting the Foundation's work to support and empower street-connected children.

Mr. Semeh explained that the “Pathways to My Future” vision board activity was designed to help the children reflect on their dreams, understand the skills and education needed to achieve them, and identify practical steps they could begin taking now.

He said the exercise was not intended to tell children what to become but to create a safe and encouraging space for them to express and plan their aspirations. “Don’t tell children what to dream. Help them discover, express and plan their dreams,” he said.

The programme also featured representatives from Kempinski Hotel, supporting partners of the program.

David Dayina, a Sales Executive at Kempinski Hotel, spoke to the children about career development, purpose and the importance of remaining open to opportunities.

He encouraged them not to be discouraged if they had not yet figured out exactly what they wanted to become, but rather to continue exploring, learning, building relationships and gaining experience.

One of the beneficiaries of the intervention, Mary Lamptey, a student of the Accra Technical University, expressed gratitude to SCEF and its partners for the support, saying the assistance had given her an opportunity to pursue her education and work towards a better future.

“I am very grateful to SCEF, Rotary Club of Accra Airport, and everyone who has supported us throughout our journey. Their support has helped us to continue our education and believe that, regardless of where you come from, you can work hard and achieve your dreams,” she said.

Ghana News.title: NPP begins vetting of 47 national officer aspirants Monday
Ghana News.content:
The vetting of 47 aspirants contesting the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) 2026 National Officers Elections begins on Monday, August 31, following the closure of nominations on Saturday.

The vetting, which will run until Thursday, September 3, is the next major stage in the party’s internal electoral process.

The National Officers Elections Committee (NOEC) said 47 of the 50 aspirants who purchased nomination forms successfully filed their completed forms before the 6:00 p.m. deadline on Saturday, August 29.

Three aspirants, however, did not complete the filing process.

They are Bernard Antwi Boasiako, who intended to contest the National Chairperson position; Evans Kodom, who sought to become National Communications Director; and Perpetual Ekua Lomokie Akwada, who purchased a form to contest the National Women Organiser position.

Mr Boasiako formally withdrew his candidature, while Mr Kodom stepped out during the filing of Dennis Miracles Aboagye’s nomination.

Ms Akwada, on the other hand, failed to submit her completed forms before the deadline.

As a result, Mr Aboagye is now the only aspirant for the National Communications Director position and will proceed to the vetting stage as a potentially unopposed candidate, subject to successfully completing the vetting process and satisfying all applicable requirements.

Vetting schedule

The four-day exercise will be conducted according to the various positions being contested.

Candidates for National Chairperson, General Secretary and National Treasurer will appear before the Vetting Committee on Monday.

National Vice Chairperson aspirants will follow on Tuesday, while candidates for National Organiser and National Youth Organiser will be vetted on Wednesday.

Aspirants for National Communications Director, National Nasara Organiser and National Women Organiser will appear before the committee on Thursday.

The Vetting Committee is chaired by former Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Cecilia Abena Dapaah.

The exercise will determine whether the 47 aspirants who successfully filed their nominations meet the requirements to proceed to the next stage of the party’s electoral process.

Three aspirants bow out

The completion of the filing process has reduced the number of active aspirants from the initial 50 who purchased nomination forms to 47.

Mr Boasiako’s withdrawal means the race for National Chairperson will proceed without his candidature, while Mr Kodom’s decision to step aside leaves Mr Aboagye as the sole candidate for National Communications Director.

Ms Akwada’s failure to submit her completed forms before the deadline similarly brings her bid for National Women Organiser to an end.

The NOEC has urged all aspirants and their supporters to conduct themselves in a manner that promotes party unity as the electoral process progresses.

It said it remained committed to ensuring an “orderly, fair, transparent and credible” process and called on all stakeholders to have confidence in the process.

The vetting is expected to provide the first formal test for the 47 aspirants seeking to become the NPP’s next national officers as the party continues its reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general election.

Ghana News.title: BoG inaugurates committee to probe seized foreign currency at Ghana’s borders
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has inaugurated a Preliminary Investigation Committee on Seized Foreign Currency as part of efforts to address the movement of undeclared foreign currency through Ghana’s airports and border points.

The initiative, according to the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, is intended to close a significant gap in Ghana’s financial system by strengthening mechanisms for monitoring and investigating foreign currency seized by the authorities.

He said substantial amounts of foreign currency were reportedly moving through the country’s borders without the required declaration.

Dr Asiama said undeclared currency flows posed risks to the integrity of Ghana’s financial sector, creating opportunities for money laundering, tax evasion and other illicit financial activities.

“Undeclared currency flows create room for money laundering, tax evasion and other illicit activity,” he said.

He added that such movements also weaken the financial intelligence available to authorities to monitor the financial system, while currency moved outside declared channels diverts funds away from the formal market.

The Bank of Ghana is working with the Ghana Revenue Authority, Ghana Airports Company Limited, National Security, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), the Financial Intelligence Centre and the Attorney General’s Office to safeguard Ghana’s borders, markets and resources.

Ghana News.title: Fix Tema Port, roads to cut logistics costs and boost trade — Oro Oil CEO, Maxwell Commey
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of Oro Oil Ghana Limited, Maxwell Commey.

Chief Executive Officer of Oro Oil Ghana Limited, Maxwell Commey, has called for urgent and coordinated action to address congestion, high logistics costs and weak inland connectivity affecting Ghana’s ports, particularly the Tema Port.

Mr Commey said the challenges were increasing the cost of doing business, constraining trade and limiting opportunities for job creation.

In a statement issued on Saturday, August 29, he said Ghana could improve the efficiency of its logistics system through targeted infrastructure upgrades, digitalisation, stronger private-sector participation and better coordination among agencies operating along the trade corridor.

“Ghana’s ports, particularly Tema, continue to grapple with congestion, high logistics costs and weak inland connectivity,” he said.

“These issues are not abstract for exporters and logistics players. For agro-industrial firms such as Oro Oil Ghana, whose palm-oil and related operations depend on reliable, lower-cost movement of goods, they directly affect competitiveness, planning and job creation.”

Roads key to easing port congestion

Mr Commey said rising trade volumes had placed increasing pressure on Tema’s landside operations, resulting in delays, yard congestion and higher costs for businesses and consumers.

He said congestion was being worsened by empty-container backlogs and heavy traffic around the port enclave, while poorly maintained access roads were contributing to accidents, vehicle damage and higher operating costs for freight operators.

“Every delay becomes a cost. A missing document or a container that remains too long in the yard leads to additional charges that are passed on,” he said.

Mr Commey therefore called for port access roads, particularly routes serving the Tema Harbour area, to be treated as an integral part of Ghana’s logistics infrastructure and prioritised for rehabilitation and capacity upgrades.

Align infrastructure with export ambitions

He also urged the government to align infrastructure investments with Ghana’s export and industrialisation ambitions.

According to him, reliable and affordable logistics would benefit exporters of palm oil, cocoa, other agricultural products and manufactured goods by reducing demurrage and inventory costs while improving the predictability of supply chains.

He said such investments would also support job creation in logistics, trucking, cargo handling and related services.

“The way forward is system-wide and coordinated,” Mr Commey said.

“Ghana should prioritise and fund integrated corridor projects that combine roads, rail and dry-port links, with clear maintenance regimes and public-private partnerships where appropriate.”

Push for digitalisation, private-sector participation

Mr Commey further called for greater use of digital systems and increased private-sector participation in port operations and related services.

He said coordination among the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority, Ghana Revenue Authority’s Customs Division, roads and highways authorities and private operators must also be strengthened to improve information sharing and accountability.

He proposed that progress should be measured through indicators such as reduced cargo dwell times, lower logistics costs, greater predictability for shippers and increased export volumes and job creation.

“From the practical perspective of an exporter whose operations depend on efficient freight movement, the payoff is straightforward: goods move at the right time and at lower cost,” he said.

“Inputs reach factories and farms more reliably; exports reach markets more competitively.”

Mr Commey said fixing the country’s inland connectivity and road infrastructure would strengthen businesses and improve Ghana’s position as a regional trade gateway.

“Ghana already has the ports and the trade ambition. Completing the inland connectivity and road pieces — transforming bottlenecks into reliable flow — is the decisive next step,” he said.

About Oro Oil Ghana Limited

Oro Oil Ghana Limited is an integrated agro-industrial company focused on oil-palm cultivation and processing.

The company says it is committed to operational excellence, international best practices, job creation and export growth.

Ghana News.title: GIPA CEO calls for stronger coordination to provide a clearer picture of investment activity
Ghana News.content:
Simon Madjie

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has called for stronger coordination among institutions to provide a clearer picture of investment activity in Ghana.

He said Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) went beyond cash inflows to include investments in machinery, equipment, raw materials and other components.

Mr. Madjie made the remarks in Accra at the unveiling of the 2025 Annual Investment Report on Friday, August 21, 2026.

The report, the first-ever FDI report compiled by GIPA, recorded US$2.62 billion in FDI in 2025.

The report was jointly compiled by GIPA, the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of Ghana, the Petroleum Commission and the Ghana Free Zones Authority.

It covers investment activity and opportunities across the economy. The launch brought together key stakeholders in Ghana’s investment ecosystem, including Dr Johnson Pandit Asiamah, Governor of the Bank of Ghana; Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry; and Emeafa Hardcastle, Chief Executive Officer of the Petroleum Commission.

Ghana secured US$ 2.6 billion in Foreign Direct Investment in 2025, compared to US$ 651.7 million in 2024.

The report revealed that “the 2025” marked a turning point in Ghana’s investment journey. “Following a period of significant macroeconomic adjustment, Ghana has made progress toward restoring stability”.

The report also believed that Ghana’s deepened global investment engagement also played a significant role in the pick-up in investments and FDIs, as targeted missions and strategic partnerships across Asia, Europe, and Africa played major roles.

New Projects

The report showed that the US$ 2.62 billion recorded in FDI inflows, was across 245 new projects and existing companies, which the report says reflects sustained investor interest in Ghana.

New investments projects accounted for the majority of inflows, completed by significant capital injections in the petroleum and free zones sectors.

At the macro level, balance of payments data showed that FDIs rose to US$1.91 billion, driven largely by reinvested earnings (95.4 %), an indication of strong investor retention and confidence.

Ghana News.title: Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers reject claims he is avoiding service on Sammy Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
Lawyers for Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin have rejected claims that their client is delaying or avoiding service of a writ on Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi in a defamation suit.

Dehyena Chambers, representing Mr Afenyo-Markin, says the writ was served on Mr Gyamfi’s lawyers after they formally notified the High Court that they had his “express instructions and authority” to accept service on his behalf.

The clarification follows an earlier report that Mr Gyamfi had authorised his lawyers, Ayine & Partners, to receive the writ and accompanying processes in the suit filed by Mr Afenyo-Markin.

Read Also: Defamation suit: Sammy Gyamfi authorises his lawyers to write to High Court to receive writ

In a statement dated Saturday, August 29, Dehyena Chambers said the writ was filed on August 24, 2026, and that two days later, Ayine & Partners wrote to the Registrar of the High Court, General Division, Accra, indicating that they had authority to accept service on Mr Gyamfi’s behalf.

According to the lawyers, a court bailiff subsequently served the writ on the law firm.

“On 26th August 2026, an Accra-based law firm by name Ayine & Partners, per a supposed lawyer named Seth Nyaaba Esq., wrote to the Registrar of the High Court informing him that the law firm had Mr Sammy Gyamfi’s ‘express instructions and authority’ to accept service of the writ on his behalf,” the statement said.

“It was with this understanding that a bailiff from the registry of the court duly served the Writ on the firm,” it added.

Lawyers say writ was later returned

Dehyena Chambers, however, said Mr Gyamfi’s lawyers returned the writ to the court registry on August 27, claiming that their client had changed his mind about service through the firm.

The lawyers further alleged that a subsequent attempt by the court bailiff to serve Mr Gyamfi personally at his office was unsuccessful.

“On that same day when the Bailiff then attempted personal service on Mr Sammy Gyamfi at his office, he refused to accept the service of writ and instructed his security personnel to send the bailiff out of the building,” the statement said.

The law firm therefore described as “untrue” claims that Mr Afenyo-Markin was avoiding service.

“It therefore cannot be the Plaintiff who is avoiding service of the writ on the Defendant as alleged on social media. This is a muddling of the rules of civil law practice in Ghana which must be disregarded,” it stated.

Lawyers cite High Court rules

Dehyena Chambers also cited Order 7, Rule 12(2) of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), arguing that service on a lawyer who has undertaken in writing to accept service on behalf of a defendant amounts to valid service.

The provision states that where a lawyer undertakes in writing to accept service of a writ on behalf of a defendant, the writ is deemed to have been duly served when it is served on that lawyer.

On that basis, Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers maintain that Mr Gyamfi has already been validly served.

“In any event, under Order 7, rule 12(2) of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 C. I. 47, a writ is duly served once it is delivered to a lawyer who has undertaken in writing to accept service on behalf of a client. Accordingly, Mr Sammy Gyamfi has been validly served,” the statement said.

The lawyers urged those disputing the validity of the service to desist, saying the correspondence between the parties and the bailiff’s official record would establish what occurred.

“Whatever be the situation, once his solicitors accepted the writ, Mr Sammy Gyamfi is fixed with Knowledge of the writ against him and is required by law to file his appearance and defence to the suit before the Court,” the statement added.

Background to the defamation suit

Mr Afenyo-Markin filed the suit at the Accra High Court on August 24 following comments made by Mr Gyamfi during the August 22 edition of JoyNews’ Newsfile programme.

The Minority Leader alleges that Mr Gyamfi defamed him by describing him as an “extortionist” during a discussion concerning GoldBod and reported losses associated with the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

Mr Afenyo-Markin is suing Mr Gyamfi and Multimedia Group Limited and is seeking damages, a retraction and apology, as well as an injunction against further publication of the alleged defamatory statements.

The dispute followed weeks of exchanges between the two politicians over the performance of the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme and questions raised by the Minority Leader about reported losses linked to the programme.

Mr Gyamfi’s August 26 notice through Ayine & Partners had indicated that he was willing to receive the court processes through his lawyers, with the notice specifically authorising the firm to accept service on his behalf.

The latest statement from Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers now introduces a dispute over whether that written authorisation resulted in valid service and whether the subsequent return of the writ affects the status of the proceedings.

The substantive case is yet to be determined by the court.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
